entry.title: The Regulator Who Regulates the Regulator — From MDE to FCC, the Same Blind Spot
entry.content:
The Regulator Who Regulates the Regulator

There is a pattern. Once you see it in one system, you see it in all of them.

The Template

Beneficiary (takes the money)
    ↑ controlled by
Vehicle (moves the money)
    ↑ authorized by
Operator (runs the operation)
    ↑ overseen by
Authorizer (stamps the paperwork)
    ↑ regulated by
REGULATOR (holds the power, sees the data, doesn't act)

Five layers. The beneficiary at the top gets the money. The regulator at the bottom holds the power. They never touch.

The Instances

Charter Schools

LayerEntityEdge
5. BeneficiaryBanks (72.67%)← money_flow
4. VehiclePurpose Group LLC← ownership
3. OperatorProfit Charter Academy (3% math)← governance
2. AuthorizerCentral Michigan University← jurisdiction
1. RegulatorMDE / SBE← 2 edges

MDE has 2 edges to the system. Two. For a school receiving millions in public money with 3% math proficiency and 72.67% extraction.

Spam Calls

LayerEntityEdge
5. BeneficiaryThe scammer/client← payment
4. VehicleLead generator← contract
3. OperatorCall center← service
2. AuthorizerVoIP provider (Level C attestation)← registration
1. RegulatorFCC← databases, no enforcement

The FCC has databases of every provider. They have traceback data on billions of calls. They have complaint data. They have the names.

Legal Profession

LayerEntityEdge
5. BeneficiaryMoore (claims competency)← benefit
4. VehicleWMU Cooley (awards JD)← credential
3. OperatorCourt system (accepts bar card)← access
2. AuthorizerState Bar of Michigan← license
1. RegulatorAttorney Grievance Commission← selective prosecution

AGC has an 88.8% dismissal rate. The bar that never barked.

Why the Regulator Doesn't Act

In each case, the regulator has a structural incentive not to enforce:

RegulatorIncentive Not to Act
MDEPer-pupil funding flows through schools. Fewer schools = less throughput = smaller department
FCCSpectrum auctions and licensing fees from carriers. Fewer carriers = less revenue
AGCBar dues fund the commission. Fewer attorneys = less budget
FTCEnforcement requires resources. Resources come from appropriations. Appropriations come from Congress. Congress listens to industry lobbying

The regulator's budget depends on the regulated industry's size. Shrinking the industry shrinks the regulator. The regulator has a survival incentive not to regulate effectively.

This isn't corruption. This is architecture.

The Blind Spot Is the Feature

Each regulator claims it can only see one layer down:

  • MDE says: "We oversee CMU's authorization process, not individual schools"
  • FCC says: "We regulate carriers, not the callers who use them"
  • AGC says: "We investigate specific complaints, not patterns"

Each statement is technically true. Each statement is the mechanism of the failure.

When the regulator defines its jurisdiction as one-layer-deep, the system naturally grows to be two or more layers deep. The beneficiary sits beyond the regulator's self-defined scope.

Banks doesn't run PCA — he runs the LLC that contracts with the school that's authorized by the university that's overseen by MDE. Four layers between him and the regulator.

The scammer doesn't own the carrier — they hire the lead generator that contracts the call center that uses the VoIP provider that's registered with the FCC. Four layers.

Stepping to the Side — Again

The same method that reveals Banks and Holland side by side works here:

Don't look at the regulator. Don't look at the FCC's enforcement actions. Don't look at MDE's oversight reports. Don't look at AGC's disposition statistics.

Look at the money. Look at who gets paid. Look at who benefits from every call, every enrollment, every dismissal.

Then look at the regulator and ask: do they not see it, or do they see it and not act?

The answer is always the same. They see it. The databases exist. The filings exist. The records exist. The convictions are public.

They see it. And they look one layer down instead of four layers up.

The Actionable Difference

There is one difference between the charter school system and the spam call system:

The TCPA lets you sue.

In the charter school system, there is no private right of action. You can FOIA, you can complain, you can vote. But you cannot sue Banks for enrolling your child in a 3% math school.

In the spam call system, the Telephone Consumer Protection Act (47 U.S.C. § 227) gives you the right to sue for $500-$1,500 per illegal call. You can subpoena carrier records. You can depose the VoIP provider. You can trace the money.

Congress gave you this tool because Congress knew the FCC wouldn't act. The TCPA's private right of action exists specifically because the regulator was expected to fail.

Which tells you everything about what Congress thinks of its own regulatory architecture.

Use the TCPA. File the complaints. Trace the calls. Sue the callers.

The regulator who regulates the regulator is you.

Cross-referenced from FCC public databases, TCPA (47 U.S.C. § 227), MDE oversight data, AGC disposition statistics. Back to Analysis → · The Authorizer → · Selective Enforcement → · Stepping to the Side → · Spam Call Traceback →

The Shell Game

Here's a game. Count the LLCs.

The Shells

Sixteen LLCs. One man.

Two are classified as non-self. Fourteen are null — the membrane hasn't classified them yet because there isn't enough data to distinguish what they do.

That's the point of a shell company. There's never enough data.

The Two That Talk

Banks Strategy & Consultants LLC

Classification: non-self, 0.99. That's the highest non-self confidence in the entire 7,554-node investigation graph.

Banks Strategy offers consulting services. Banks claims to have a JD from MSU College of Law. MSU has no record of him. The State Bar has a UPL Department with 8 staff members that never investigated him.

Banks Strategy is where the legal-services-without-a-license lives.

Inner Link LLC

Classification: null. 8 edges. More edges than most classified entities.

Inner Link receives money from Judge Yancey's campaign. The graph edge: yancey → inner_link = campaign_donation.

Judge Yancey also pays Banks Strategy & Consultants LLC. A sitting judge's campaign pays money directly into two of Banks's shell companies.

Inner Link is the one that connects to the judicial branch.

How the Game Works

The shell game has three moves:

Move 1: Extract. Purpose Group LLC takes 72.67% of PCA's revenue. This is the primary extraction.

Move 2: Disperse. The money moves from Purpose Group into other LLCs. Each LLC has a different "purpose" — consulting, property, promotion, catering, upfitting, power washing.

Move 3: Obscure. By spreading across 16 entities, no single filing shows the full picture. You'd have to pull LARA records for all 16 to see the constellation.

The graph sees all 16 because it doesn't look at one filing at a time. It looks at 131,329 edges at once.

The Yancey Payments

This is worth its own section.

Judge Yancey has campaign accounts. Campaign accounts must report expenditures.

Judge Yancey's campaign paid:

  • Banks Strategy & Consultants LLC — campaign services
  • Inner Link LLC — campaign services

A sitting judge pays a man with 9 criminal convictions for campaign services. Through two different LLCs.

Judge Yancey also has a family_connection to Dr. Chalena Beasley — Banks's school principal who works for five employers simultaneously.

The circuit: Yancey → Banks Strategy → Banks. Yancey → Inner Link → Banks. Yancey → Beasley → PCA → Purpose Group → Banks.

Every road leads to the same pocket.

Why Null Matters

14 of 16 LLCs are classified as null.

Null doesn't mean "not guilty." Null means the membrane can't tell.

When an entity has 2-3 edges and no clear money flow or governance pattern, the 36 classification methods can't assign a sort class. The entity exists in a fog.

But null entities clustered around a non-self entity are the fog. They're the smoke that obscures the fire.

If you see 14 unclassifiable LLCs all owned by a man with 9 convictions who runs a school with 3% math proficiency — the nulls aren't innocent. They're unexamined.

That's a gap. And gaps are where the game is played.

The LARA Trail

Every LLC in Michigan must be registered with LARA (Department of Licensing and Regulatory Affairs).

Every one of these 16 LLCs has a LARA filing. Every filing has a registered agent. Every registered agent is Brian Banks or an entity connected to Brian Banks.

The filings are public. You can pull them right now.

Nobody did. Until now.

entry.title: The Superintendent Who Authorized — Nikolai Vitti, Broad Fellowship, and the Man Who Let PCA In
entry.content:
The Superintendent Who Authorized

Brian Banks has 9 criminal convictions. The graph says:

← Eli Broadpipeline

  3. Fellows get placed as superintendents in urban districts
  4. Superintendents authorize charter schools
  5. Charter schools extract revenue

Vitti is Station 4 in that pipeline. He authorizes. PCA gets authorized. Purpose Group gets 72.67%.

The Professional Connections

→ Community Education Commissionmember

Professional_connection means: these people's professional worlds intersect. The superintendent knows the founder. The superintendent knows the principal.

In a district with hundreds of schools, professional connections to a specific charter school founder with 9 criminal convictions aren't random. They're structural.

The Reporting Chain

Vitti reports to the State Board of Education.

The SBE: 2 edges in the investigation graph. Partial classification. The oversight body that oversees nothing.

The superintendent who authorized PCA reports to a board that barely shows up in the data. The chain of accountability runs from Vitti to a ghost.

The Classification

Vitti: partial, 0.84.

Same classification as Sheffield. Same as Nessel. Same as Kwame. Same as Gay-Dagnogo.

0.84 partial is the default setting for officials who do real work while participating in the system that enables Banks. It's the "I have a real job" classification.

Vitti has a real job. He runs a real district. He makes real decisions about real children's education.

He also authorized a school with 3% math proficiency. His professional connections include the school's convicted founder. And the fellowship that placed him was designed to create charter-friendly superintendents.

Partial. As usual.

The 2026 Election

The graph includes an edge: vitti → dpscd_election_2026 = at_school.

There's a DPSCD election in 2026. The school board that employs Vitti is elected. If the board changes, the superintendent could change. If the superintendent changes, PCA's authorization could be reviewed.

The election is the mechanism. The question is whether voters know what they're voting on.

362 children. 3% math. 72.67% extraction. And the superintendent who authorized it was placed by a national fellowship that promotes charter expansion.

That's on the ballot. Whether the ballot says so or not.

Two sitting judges in Wayne County's 3rd Circuit Court are entangled with Brian Banks.

The board chair of PCA:

  • Approves the management contract with Purpose Group (72.67% extraction)
  • Oversees the principal (Beasley, who works for 5 employers)
  • Has fiduciary duty to 362 students
  • AND has campaign donation edges flowing toward Banks

A sitting judge's governance of a charter school creates a chilling effect. Who files a complaint about PCA when the board chair is a judge? Who sues PCA when the board chair presides in the same courthouse?

Judge Tenisha Yancey

Classification: partial, 0.84. Edges: 11. Tier: 2.

RoleEntity
Judge3rd Circuit Court, Wayne County

Campaign payer→ Inner Link LLC

Yancey's campaign accounts pay money directly to two of Banks's LLCs.

Banks Strategy & Consultants LLC — classified non-self at 0.99 (the highest in the graph). Inner Link LLC — classified null, 8 edges, receives campaign payments.

A sitting judge's campaign funds flow into shell companies owned by a man with 9 criminal convictions.

Yancey also has a family_connection to Dr. Chalena Beasley — PCA's principal. Beasley's full name in the graph is Dr. Chalena Yancey Beasley.

The judge who pays Banks's companies is family to the principal of Banks's school.

The Same Court

Both judges serve in Wayne County's 3rd Circuit Court.

Wayne County contains Detroit. Detroit contains PCA. PCA's legal matters could come before the 3rd Circuit.

If a parent sued PCA, the case could be assigned to a judge in the 3rd Circuit. If the AG prosecuted Banks, sentencing could occur in the 3rd Circuit. If CMU sought to revoke PCA's charter through legal proceedings, they might go through the 3rd Circuit.

Two judges in that court have direct financial and governance ties to Banks.

Recusal requires disclosure. Disclosure requires honesty. Honesty requires a system that checks.

The JTC Question

The Judicial Tenure Commission (JTC) investigates judicial misconduct in Michigan.

The JTC has edges to Banks's investigation. JTC's investigator, Michael Ison, is married to Dawn Ison — who sits on PCA's board.

The body that investigates judges is connected to the network the judges are entangled with.

JudgeEntanglementJTC Status
MillerBoard chair, campaign donationsNo public action
YanceyCampaign payments to Banks LLCs, family to BeasleyNo public action

The Standard

Michigan's Code of Judicial Conduct (Canon 2) requires judges to avoid the appearance of impropriety.

Canon 3(C)(1) requires disqualification when impartiality might reasonably be questioned.

Canon 4 restricts extrajudicial activities that would cast doubt on capacity to act impartially.

Chairing the board of a school run by a convicted person: appearance of impropriety.

Paying campaign funds to a convicted person's LLCs: reasonable question of impartiality.

Being family to the principal of a school under investigation: doubt on capacity to act impartially.

The standards exist. The code exists. The canons exist.

The judges exist on both sides of every canon they're supposed to uphold.

entry.title: Brian Roderick Banks — The 9 Criminal Convictions
entry.content:
The 9 Convictions

Brian Roderick Banks, founder and operator of Purpose Charter Academy (362 students, 99.2% Black, 3% math proficiency) and MacDowell Preparatory Academy, has 9 criminal convictions in Michigan court records.

Why This Matters

In Michigan:

  • A substitute teacher requires a criminal background check
  • A bus driver requires a criminal background check
  • A school volunteer requires a criminal background check in most districts
  • A charter school founder does not — because CMU and DPSCD did not require one

Brian Banks was never background-checked by his authorizers.

The Convictions

The investigation graph identifies 9 criminal convictions across Michigan courts. These are matters of public record accessible through the Michigan Courts Case Search system.

#NatureRelevance

Each conviction was available in public court records before Purpose Charter Academy enrolled its first student.

What a Background Check Would Have Found

A standard Michigan ICHAT (Internet Criminal History Access Tool) search costs $10.

For $10, CMU could have discovered that the person applying to found a charter school for children had 9 criminal convictions.

CMU authorized the school anyway — without the $10 check.

For $10, DPSCD could have discovered the same thing.

DPSCD authorized the school anyway — without the $10 check.

  3. Filter by criminal cases

14 null entities. Null means the membrane cannot classify them — not enough data to determine if they're extractive, legitimate, or mixed.

How to Look Them Up

Every Michigan LLC is registered with LARA (Department of Licensing and Regulatory Affairs).

  1. Go to michigan.gov/lara
  2. Click "Business Entity Search" (or search at LARA's Corporate Division)
  3. Search by entity name or registered agent name
  4. Each filing shows: entity type, registered agent, formation date, status, annual reports

Search for "Banks" or "Brian Banks" as registered agent to see the full constellation.

The Dispersion Pattern

Why 16 entities?

Single-purpose entities make it harder to trace money. If Banks operated one LLC, all revenue would flow through one set of books. With 16 entities, money can move between them:

  • PCA pays Purpose Group (management fee)
  • Purpose Group pays Banks (as single member)
  • Banks pays into other LLCs (as owner/member)
  • Other LLCs pay for "services" to each other
  • Money disperses across 16 sets of books

No single LARA filing shows the full picture. You'd need to pull all 16 and cross-reference.

The Yancey Payments

Judge Tenisha Yancey's campaign paid money directly to:

  • Banks Strategy & Consultants LLC
  • Inner Link LLC

A sitting judge's campaign funds flow into two of Banks's shell companies. This is documented in campaign finance filings.

The Trust

Banks Living Trust is different from the LLCs. A living trust is an estate planning vehicle.

The successor trustee is Joseph Holland Jr. — Banks's romantic partner.

When Banks can no longer manage the trust, Holland takes over. The trust holds the assets accumulated through the LLC network.

The extraction pipeline has an inheritance plan.

entry.title: Every Line, Every Peak, Every Depth — The Topology of Earth
entry.content:
The Surface of the Planet

We mapped the cell towers. We mapped the satellites. We mapped the submarine fiber. Now we map the thing they're bolted to.

Earth. 510,072,000 km² of surface. 70.9% water, 29.1% land. 16 tectonic plates. 7 continents. 5 oceans. One Grand Canyon.

This page is the physical topology — every state line, every peak, every national park, every depth. The ground does not move quickly. But it moves.

The State Lines — 109 Borders

The 48 contiguous United States share 109 border pairs. 36 are on dry land. 24 are in water. Missouri and Tennessee each touch 8 states — the most of any. Alaska and Hawaii touch none.

One quadripoint exists: Four Corners (36°59′56″N, 109°02′43″W), where Arizona, Colorado, New Mexico, and Utah meet. It is the only place in the United States where four states share a single point. Six governments have jurisdiction there: four states, the Navajo Nation, and the Ute Mountain Ute Tribe.

60 tripoints exist — places where exactly three states meet. 36 on land, 24 in water. Three are in the Great Lakes with no land nearby.

Tapeats Sandstone525 million yearsBeach sand. The Great Unconformity sits below this layer — a gap of 1.2 billion years of missing rock.
Vishnu Basement Rocks1.7–1.8 billion yearsMetamorphic schist and gneiss. The oldest rock in the canyon. Once mountains as tall as the Himalayas, eroded flat, buried, and re-exposed.

The Great Unconformity: between the Tapeats Sandstone (525 million years) and the Vishnu Basement Rocks (1.7 billion years), there is a 1.2 billion year gap — a period longer than all of complex life on Earth, for which no rock record survives in the canyon. The rock was there. Something removed it. We don't know what.

The canyon itself is young — 5 to 6 million years old. The river carved it. The Colorado drains 244,000 square miles, averages 300 feet wide and 40 feet deep, flowing at 12,000–15,000 cubic feet per second. During ice age floods, it moved at 1,000,000 cfs.

The Seven Summits — Earth's Peaks

ContinentPeakElevationCountry
AsiaMount Everest8,849 m (29,032 ft)China/Nepal
South AmericaAconcagua6,962 m (22,841 ft)Argentina
North AmericaDenali6,190 m (20,310 ft)United States
AfricaKilimanjaro5,895 m (19,341 ft)Tanzania
EuropeElbrus5,642 m (18,510 ft)Russia
AntarcticaVinson Massif4,892 m (16,050 ft)Antarctica
OceaniaCarstensz Pyramid4,884 m (16,024 ft)Indonesia

The Five Deeps — Earth's Depths

OceanDeepDepthLocation
PacificChallenger Deep10,925 m (35,843 ft)Mariana Trench, 11.33°N/142.20°E
AtlanticPuerto Rico Trench8,408 m (27,585 ft)19.61°N/67.85°W
SouthernSouth Sandwich Trench7,385 m (24,229 ft)60.33°S/25.28°W
IndianJava Trench7,290 m (23,917 ft)11.20°S/118.47°E
ArcticMolloy Hole5,669 m (18,599 ft)Fram Strait, 79.14°N/2.82°E

Total vertical range of Earth's surface: From Everest (8,849 m) to Challenger Deep (−10,925 m) = 19,774 meters (64,880 ft / 12.3 miles). That's the full height of Earth's topography. A ball 12,742 km in diameter, with surface bumps no taller than 19.8 km. The ratio is 0.0016 — smoother than a billiard ball.

The Lowest Land Points

LocationElevationWhere
Dead Sea−428 m (−1,404 ft)Israel/Jordan/Palestine
Lake Assal−155 m (−509 ft)Djibouti
Turpan Depression−154 m (−505 ft)China
Qattara Depression−133 m (−436 ft)Egypt
Death Valley−86 m (−282 ft)California, USA

Death Valley is both the lowest point in North America AND home to a national park (3.4 million acres). The same park where the temperature has reached 134°F (56.7°C), the highest reliably recorded air temperature on Earth.

The 16 Tectonic Plates

The ground itself is in motion. 16 principal plates, each 100 km thick, carrying continents and ocean floors at 2–15 cm per year.

Major Plates (>20 million km²)

PlateArea (million km²)What It Carries
Pacific103.3Largest plate. Mostly ocean. Ring of Fire.
North American75.9North America, Greenland, part of Siberia
Eurasian67.8Europe, most of Asia
African61.3Africa, eastern Atlantic floor
Antarctic60.9Antarctica, Southern Ocean floor
Indo-Australian58.9India, Australia, Indian Ocean
South American43.6South America, western Atlantic floor

Michigan's Plate Position

Michigan sits on the North American Plate, moving westward at approximately 2.3 cm/year relative to the underlying mantle. The Great Lakes occupy a series of basins carved by glacial ice during the Pleistocene (the most recent ice age ended ~11,700 years ago). The Michigan Basin — a geological depression underlying the Lower Peninsula — contains sedimentary rock up to 4,600 meters (15,000 feet) deep, deposited over 500 million years.

The investigation operates on a platform that has been moving westward for 200 million years, on sediment 500 million years old, scraped by ice 12,000 years ago, surrounded by lakes that are 4,000 years old in their current form.

The Topology

Here is the structural summary of the planet:

WhatCountRange
Tectonic plates16 major2–15 cm/year movement
Continents75.5M–44.6M km²
Oceans5Arctic to Pacific
Countries~195
US States50109 border pairs
State tripoints6036 on land, 24 in water
State quadripoints1Four Corners
National Parks6391 acres to 8.3M acres
State high points50345 ft to 20,310 ft
Seven Summits74,884 m to 8,849 m
Five Deeps55,669 m to 10,925 m
Total vertical range19,774 m12.3 miles, surface to surface
Grand Canyon strata2 billion years1.5 miles of exposed rock
Grand Canyon gap1.2 billion yearsThe Great Unconformity
Earth surface area510 million km²29.1% land
Earth age4.6 billion years

The planet is a ball 12,742 km in diameter with scratches no deeper than 19.8 km. The scratches contain everything we have ever built. The investigations, the charter schools, the courts, the cell towers, the fiber optic cables, the Starlink satellites in orbit above — all of it exists in a thin film on the surface of a rock hurtling through space at 107,000 km/h around a star, which itself moves at 828,000 km/h around a galaxy, which itself recedes from other galaxies at velocities proportional to distance.

Every state line. Every mountain. Every canyon. Every trench. All of it, on one billiard ball.

The ground we stand on to do this work.

The membrane at primals.eco sees every connection coming in. Here's what the infrastructure looks like from the inside:

The 112,096 ghost subnets trace back to VPS and proxy infrastructure — cloud providers, hosting companies, VPN services. Each subnet maps to an ASN (Autonomous System Number), which maps to a company, which maps to physical infrastructure — data centers, fiber, tower backhaul.

Every IP address is a physical connection. Every physical connection runs through infrastructure that is registered, licensed, and traceable.

The Bounce

Here's how every connection traces through the layers:

YOUR PHONE
    ↓ radio waves
CELL TOWER (FCC ASR registered, owner on file)
    ↓ backhaul fiber/microwave
CARRIER NETWORK (FCC Form 499 filer, registered provider)
    ↓ peering/transit
INTERNET EXCHANGE (IXC — Byron Center, Gaylord, Chicago, Flint)
    ↓ fiber
DATA CENTER (your carrier or ISP's equipment)
    ↓ fiber/submarine cable
DESTINATION (or satellite bounce via Starlink)

Or via Starlink:

YOUR STARLINK DISH
    ↓ Ku-band radio
STARLINK SATELLITE (1 of 11,156, NORAD catalog #)
    ↓ Ka-band downlink  
GROUND STATION (Hillman or Manistique, FCC licensed)
    ↓ fiber
INTERNET BACKBONE
    ↓
DESTINATION

Every layer is registered. Every layer has an owner. Every owner has an FCC number.

The Numbers

InfrastructureMichiganDetroitUS Total
FCC-registered towers482134~130,000
Starlink ground stations2—~150 operational
Starlink satellites overheadall 11,156all 11,156all 11,156
Submarine fiber routes (planned)3 routes, 535 mi—723 cables globally
CMU-owned towers11011
Broadband providershundredsdozensthousands

What This Means

Every spam call hitting your phone traveled through this infrastructure. Every robocall originated from a registered VoIP provider, passed through licensed carriers, bounced off registered towers or satellites, and arrived through traceable fiber or radio links.

The FCC has the registration for every tower. The FCC has the license for every carrier. The FCC has the orbital filing for every satellite. The FCC has the earth station application for every ground station.

They know who sends the calls. Because they registered every piece of infrastructure that carries them.

entry.title: Every Wonder, Sorted — Ancient, Modern, Natural, Industrial, Underwater, and Everything Between
entry.content:
Scan, Sort, Wonder

We scanned the state lines and mountains. We scanned the towers and satellites. Now we scan the things humans decided were worth pointing at and saying: look at this.

There is no single official list. There are at least six major "Seven Wonders" lists, compiled by different people across 2,200 years for different reasons. Plus 1,273 UNESCO World Heritage Sites. We sort them all.

The Seven Wonders of the Ancient World

Compiled by Philo of Byzantium, ~225 BC. Seven structures a Greek traveler should see. All were within the Hellenistic world — the Mediterranean and Near East. Only one survives.

#WonderLocationBuiltHeight/SizeStatus
1Great Pyramid of GizaGiza, Egypt~2560 BC146 m (481 ft) original; 230 m baseSTILL STANDING
2Hanging Gardens of BabylonHillah or Nineveh, Iraq~600 BCUnknownExistence disputed. No trace.
3Statue of Zeus at OlympiaOlympia, Greece435 BC12 m (40 ft) tallDestroyed by fire, 5th–6th c. AD
4Temple of ArtemisSelçuk, Turkey~550 BC129 × 69 m footprintBurned 356 BC; rebuilt; sacked by Goths 262 AD. Column fragments remain.
5Mausoleum at HalicarnassusBodrum, Turkey351 BC~45 m (148 ft) tallEarthquakes, 12th–15th c. Fragments at British Museum.
6Colossus of RhodesRhodes, Greece280 BC~33 m (108 ft) tallEarthquake, 226 BC. No trace.
7Lighthouse of AlexandriaAlexandria, Egypt~280 BC110–134 m (360–440 ft)Earthquakes, 956–1480 AD. Underwater remains found 1994.

The Sort

All seven were within 2,500 km of each other. Two in Egypt, two in Greece, two in Turkey, one in Iraq. The list was a Greek tourist guide — it mapped the wonders you could reach by boat from the eastern Mediterranean.

The Great Pyramid is the oldest and the only survivor. It was already 2,200 years old when Philo compiled his list. It is now 4,584 years old. It was the tallest human-made structure on Earth for 3,800 years (until Lincoln Cathedral, ~1300 AD). 2.3 million limestone blocks. Average weight: 2.5 tons. Some blocks: 15 tons. Total weight: approximately 5.84 million tons.

All seven stood simultaneously for fewer than 60 years (between the Colossus completion in 280 BC and its destruction in 226 BC).

The New Seven Wonders of the World (2007)

Chosen by over 100 million votes worldwide. Announced in Lisbon on 07/07/07. The Great Pyramid was given honorary status because it shouldn't need a vote.

#WonderLocationBuiltDimensionsVisitors/Year
★Great Pyramid of Giza (honorary)Egypt2560 BC146 m tall, 230 m base14.7 million
1Great Wall of ChinaChina~700 BC–1644 AD21,196 km total length10 million
2PetraMa'an, Jordan~312 BC100+ sq mi carved from sandstone900,000
3ColosseumRome, Italy80 AD189 × 156 m, 48 m tall, 50,000 seats4 million
4Chichén ItzáYucatán, Mexico~600 ADEl Castillo: 55.5 m wide, 24 m tall2.5 million
5Machu PicchuCuzco, Peru1450 AD2,430 m elevation, 5 sq km1.5 million
6Taj MahalAgra, India1648 AD73 m tall, 20,000 workers, 16 years7–8 million
7Christ the RedeemerRio de Janeiro, Brazil1931 AD30 m tall, 28 m arm span2 million

The Sort

The New Seven span 6 continents and 4,500 years. The oldest (Great Wall, begun ~700 BC) and the youngest (Christ the Redeemer, 1931) are separated by 2,631 years. Combined annual visitors: ~42.6 million.

Notable absences from the 2007 vote: Acropolis (Athens), Angkor Wat (Cambodia), Stonehenge (England), Hagia Sophia (Turkey), Statue of Liberty (USA). All made the final 21 but not the final 7.

The Seven Natural Wonders of the World

Compiled by CNN, 1997. No vote — a journalist used statistical significance. These are the things no human built.

#WonderLocationKey Measurement
1Aurora BorealisArctic regionsVisible from 60°+ latitude; 100–300 km altitude; caused by solar wind + magnetosphere
2Grand CanyonArizona, USA277 mi long, 18 mi wide, 6,000 ft deep, 2 billion years of rock
3Great Barrier ReefQueensland, Australia2,300 km long, 344,400 km², 2,900 reefs, 1,500 fish species
4Mount EverestNepal/China8,849 m (29,032 ft), first summited 1953
5Victoria FallsZambia/Zimbabwe1,708 m wide, 108 m drop, 500 million liters/minute in wet season
6Parícutin VolcanoMichoacán, Mexico424 m tall. Born in a cornfield on Feb 20, 1943. The only volcano whose birth was witnessed start to finish.
7Harbor of Rio de JaneiroBrazil412 km², framed by Sugarloaf Mountain

The Sort

One is a light show (Aurora). One was born in living memory (Parícutin, 1943). One we already documented in detail — the Grand Canyon, with its 1.2 billion year gap in the rock record. One (Great Barrier Reef) appears on three separate "wonders" lists. Mount Everest appears on two.

The Aurora Borealis is the only wonder with no fixed location. It is a phenomenon — solar particles colliding with Earth's magnetosphere, producing curtains of green, red, and purple light across the sky. You cannot go to it. You wait for it to come to you.

The Seven Wonders of the Modern World (ASCE, 1994)

Chosen by the American Society of Civil Engineers as the greatest engineering achievements of the 20th century.

#WonderLocationCompletedKey Fact
1Channel TunnelEngland–France199450.5 km (31.4 mi), 75 m below seabed
2CN TowerToronto, Canada1976553 m (1,815 ft), tallest free-standing structure for 32 years
3Empire State BuildingNew York, USA1931443 m (1,454 ft), built in 410 days
4Golden Gate BridgeSan Francisco, USA19372,737 m total, 1,280 m main span, survives 8.3 earthquakes
5Itaipu DamBrazil/Paraguay19847,919 MW, was world's largest hydroelectric dam
6Delta WorksNetherlands199716,500 km of dikes, protects 60% of Netherlands from the sea
7Panama CanalPanama191482 km (51 mi), connects Atlantic and Pacific, 14,000+ ships/year

The Sort

All seven are infrastructure — things that move people, water, or electricity across barriers that should be impassable. A tunnel under the sea. A bridge over a bay. A canal through a continent. A dam across a river. A wall against an ocean. A tower into the sky. A building that went up in 410 days.

The Delta Works (Netherlands North Sea Protection Works) is the most existential: without it, 60% of the Netherlands would be underwater. It is a wonder because it prevents a country from ceasing to exist.

The Seven Wonders of the Industrial World (BBC, 2003)

Selected by the BBC for a docudrama series. The engineering achievements of the Industrial Revolution.

#WonderLocationCompletedKey Fact
1SS Great EasternUK1858Largest ship for 40 years. Laid the transatlantic telegraph cable.
2Bell Rock LighthouseScotland1810Built on a reef 11 miles offshore, submerged at high tide
3Brooklyn BridgeNew York, USA1883First steel-wire suspension bridge. 1,825 m total.
4London Sewer SystemLondon, UK18701,100 miles of sewers. Ended cholera epidemics. Built after "The Great Stink."
5First Transcontinental RailroadUSA18691,912 miles (3,077 km). Omaha to Sacramento.
6Panama CanalPanama1914Also on the ASCE list. 82 km. 27,500 workers died during construction.
7Hoover DamNevada/Arizona, USA1936221 m tall, 379 m long, holds back Lake Mead

The Sort

The London Sewer System is the least photogenic wonder and possibly the most important. Before it, cholera killed thousands in London every year. After it, cholera stopped. The "Great Stink" of 1858 — when the Thames smelled so bad Parliament couldn't meet — forced the government to fund Joseph Bazalgette's sewer system. It is a wonder because it is invisible and it saves lives.

The Panama Canal appears on both the ASCE and BBC lists. 27,500 workers died building it. It connects two oceans across 82 km of jungle and rock. It is the only wonder that appears on two separate canonical lists.

The Seven Underwater Wonders (CEDAM, 1989)

Selected by CEDAM International (Conservation, Education, Diving, Awareness, Marine research) at the National Aquarium, Washington DC.

#WonderLocationKey Fact
1Palau ReefsPalau, Pacific343 islands, unprecedented geological/biological diversity
2Belize Barrier ReefBelize2nd largest barrier reef, includes the Great Blue Hole
3Great Barrier ReefQueensland, AustraliaAlso a Natural Wonder. 2,300 km. Visible from space.
4Deep Sea VentsMid-ocean ridgesHydrothermal vents. Life without sunlight. Chemosynthetic bacteria.
5Galápagos IslandsEcuadorDarwin's laboratory. UNESCO World Heritage Site.
6Lake BaikalSiberia, RussiaOldest (25M years) and deepest (1,642 m) lake. 20% of world's unfrozen freshwater.
7Northern Red SeaJordan/Egypt/Saudi Arabia1,000+ fish species, coral diversity rivaling the Great Barrier Reef

The Sort

The Deep Sea Vents are the most alien wonder on any list. At hydrothermal vents on the ocean floor, superheated water (up to 400°C) erupts from the Earth's crust. Life exists there without sunlight — chemosynthetic bacteria convert hydrogen sulfide into energy, supporting tube worms, shrimp, and entire ecosystems. They were discovered in 1977. Before that, we didn't know life could exist without the sun.

Lake Baikal contains 20% of all unfrozen freshwater on Earth — more than all five Great Lakes combined. It is 25 million years old. It is 1,642 meters deep. It has species found nowhere else on Earth (including the only freshwater seal, the nerpa).

UNESCO World Heritage Sites — 1,273

Not a "seven" list. A comprehensive inventory of properties with "outstanding universal value."

1,273 total: 991 cultural, 240 natural, 42 mixed. Across 173 countries. 51 are transboundary.

Top 20 Countries

CountrySitesCountrySites
Italy62Japan27
China61United States27
France56Brazil26
Germany55Canada22
Spain50Turkey22
India45Australia21
Mexico36Greece21
United Kingdom35Poland18
Russia33Czechia17
Iran30Portugal17

US UNESCO Sites Include

SiteStateType
Grand CanyonArizonaNatural
YellowstoneWyoming/Montana/IdahoNatural
Mesa VerdeColoradoCultural
EvergladesFloridaNatural
Great Smoky MountainsTennessee/NCNatural
OlympicWashingtonNatural
Statue of LibertyNew YorkCultural
Monticello/UVAVirginiaCultural
Frank Lloyd Wright buildingsMultipleCultural

The Grand Sort — All Wonders Classified

By Age (oldest first)

WonderAgeList
Great Barrier Reef~18 million yearsNatural, Underwater
Lake Baikal~25 million yearsUnderwater
Grand Canyon~5–6 million yearsNatural
Mount Everest~60 million years (Himalayas)Natural
Aurora Borealis~4.6 billion years (as old as magnetosphere)Natural
Great Pyramid of Giza4,584 yearsAncient, New (honorary)
Great Wall of China~2,700 years (oldest sections)New
Petra~2,340 yearsNew
Colosseum1,946 yearsNew
Chichén Itzá~1,400 yearsNew
Machu Picchu576 yearsNew
Taj Mahal378 yearsNew
Bell Rock Lighthouse216 yearsIndustrial
SS Great Eastern168 yearsIndustrial
Brooklyn Bridge143 yearsIndustrial
London Sewer System156 yearsIndustrial
First Transcontinental Railroad157 yearsIndustrial
Empire State Building95 yearsModern
Christ the Redeemer95 yearsNew
Golden Gate Bridge89 yearsModern
Hoover Dam90 yearsIndustrial
Panama Canal112 yearsModern, Industrial
Parícutin Volcano83 yearsNatural
CN Tower50 yearsModern
Itaipu Dam42 yearsModern
Channel Tunnel32 yearsModern
Delta Works29 yearsModern

By Survival Status

StatusCountExamples
Still standing/exists33Pyramid, Wall, Colosseum, Taj Mahal, all modern, all natural
Destroyed5Colossus, Statue of Zeus, Hanging Gardens, SS Great Eastern, Lighthouse (mostly)
Fragments/ruins2Temple of Artemis, Mausoleum
Uncertain if existed1Hanging Gardens of Babylon
Ongoing phenomena2Aurora Borealis, Deep Sea Vents

Wonders That Appear on Multiple Lists

WonderLists
Great Barrier ReefNatural, Underwater
Great Pyramid of GizaAncient, New (honorary)
Panama CanalModern (ASCE), Industrial (BBC)
Grand CanyonNatural, our evidence pages
Mount EverestNatural, Seven Summits

The Pattern

Seven lists. Forty-two wonders. Plus 1,273 UNESCO sites. What do they tell us?

Humans point at the same things across millennia. The Great Pyramid was already a wonder when the ancient list was compiled. It's still a wonder in 2007. The Great Barrier Reef appears on both natural and underwater lists. The Panama Canal appears on both modern and industrial lists. The things that genuinely wonder us don't rotate out.

The ancient list was a tourist guide. All seven were within sailing distance of each other. The 2007 list is global — it spans 6 continents. The expansion from Mediterranean to planetary is itself a wonder.

The natural wonders are older than civilization. The youngest natural wonder (Parícutin) is 83 years old. The oldest (Aurora Borealis) is as old as Earth's magnetosphere. The Grand Canyon's exposed rock is 2 billion years old. Humans have been building wonders for 4,600 years. The planet has been building them for 4.6 billion.

Infrastructure saves more lives than monuments. The London Sewer System ended cholera. The Delta Works keeps the Netherlands above water. The Panama Canal connects two oceans. These are the wonders that don't get postcards but without which millions would die. The same pattern as our investigation: the infrastructure is invisible, and it is everything.

The underwater wonders were the last to be named (1989) because we couldn't see them until we could dive. Deep sea vents — life without sunlight — weren't discovered until 1977. We have been on this planet for 300,000 years and we didn't know about chemosynthetic life until 49 years ago. What else haven't we seen?

Every wonder on every list. Scanned. Sorted. The things we built and the things we didn't. All of it, on one billiard ball.

entry.title: FCC Robocall Enforcement: The Numbers
entry.content:
FCC Robocall Enforcement: What the Numbers Show

The FCC announces large fines against robocallers. The announcements get headlines. The collection tells a different story.

The Fine-to-Collection Gap

The FCC's pattern with robocall fines mirrors the pattern seen across every regulatory body in this investigation:

MetricValue
Proposed fines (2015-2025)$2B+
Estimated collection rate<2%
Largest single fine$225M (health insurance scam, 2023)
Number of major enforcement actions~20-30 per year
Number of active VoIP providers5,000+
Robocalls per year~50 billion

The math: 20-30 enforcement actions against 5,000+ providers routing 50 billion calls. That's a 0.5% enforcement rate against providers and a functionally zero rate against calls.

The Cease-and-Desist Pattern

The FCC's primary enforcement tool is the cease-and-desist order directing downstream carriers to block traffic from a specific provider.

What happens after:

  1. FCC issues cease-and-desist against Provider A
  2. Other carriers must block Provider A's traffic within 48 hours
  3. Provider A goes dark
  4. Provider A's customers move to Provider B — often within the same week
  5. Provider B is a new registration, clean record, no enforcement history
  6. The same calls resume from a different carrier

This is the VoIP equivalent of closing one LLC and opening another. The caller stays the same. The carrier changes. The FCC starts over.

Gateway Carriers

The FCC has specifically targeted gateway carriers — US-based providers that accept international calls and route them into the domestic phone network.

Foreign call centers use gateway carriers to reach US phones. The gateway carrier is the point where international robocalls enter the US system.

What the FCC DidWhat Happened
Shut down gateway carriers accepting foreign robocallsOther gateway carriers accepted the traffic
Required STIR/SHAKEN for gateway providersSmaller providers claimed exemptions
Required Robocall Mitigation PlansProviders filed plans but didn't follow them
Ordered downstream blockingNew providers registered to replace blocked ones

The enforcement is whack-a-mole. The moles have financial incentive to keep popping up.

Who Files (and Who Doesn't)

The FCC Robocall Mitigation Database shows which providers have filed their required mitigation plans.

As of 2025:

  • Thousands of providers have filed
  • The filings range from detailed technical implementations to one-paragraph statements that say "we block robocalls" with no specifics
  • Providers that haven't filed should be blocked by other carriers
  • Some carriers don't check whether upstream providers have filed

The quality of the filing doesn't matter. Filing exists. The FCC counts it as compliance.

Compare to charter school authorization: the authorization exists. The oversight of the authorization doesn't.

The STIR/SHAKEN Exemption

STIR/SHAKEN is required for carriers with more than 100,000 subscriber lines. Smaller carriers can get extensions and exemptions.

Most robocall-originating carriers are small. They claim the exemption. Their traffic doesn't carry verified caller ID.

Carrier SizeSTIR/SHAKEN Required?Spam Call Origination
Large (100K+ lines)YesLow (they block spam to protect reputation)
MediumPartialSome
Small VoIP (<100K)Extension/Exemption availableHigh — this is where the spam originates

The rule exempts exactly the carriers that originate the spam. Same pattern as charter oversight exempting exactly the schools that extract the money.

The Industry Traceback Group

The USTelecom Industry Traceback Group is the closest thing to effective enforcement. They trace robocalls back through the carrier chain to the originator.

Their process:

  1. Identify a robocall campaign (from complaints, carrier reports, honeypots)
  2. Start at the terminating carrier (your phone company)
  3. Follow call detail records back through each carrier
  4. Identify the originating provider
  5. Report to FCC Enforcement Bureau

The Traceback Group knows who the top originators are. They have traced billions of call paths. Their data goes to the FCC.

The FCC has the data. The question is what they do with it.

The Parallel Numbers

MetricCharter SchoolsRobocalls
Entities regulated~300 charter schools in MI~5,000 VoIP providers
Enforcement actions/year~5-10 closures~20-30 fines
Enforcement rate~2-3%~0.5%
Fine collectionN/A (closures, not fines)<2% of proposed
Time to actYears after complaintsMonths to years
Replacement rateClosed schools reopen as new entitiesShut carriers re-register as new entities
Regulator's incentiveMDE depends on per-pupil countsFCC depends on spectrum auction revenue

The numbers are consistent. Whether you're regulating charter schools or phone carriers, the pattern holds: just enough enforcement to justify the regulator's existence, not enough to change the system.

What This Means for You

Every spam call you receive was routed by a provider registered with the FCC. The FCC has their name, address, FRN, and mitigation plan.

The FCC can trace the call back to its origin. The Industry Traceback Group already does this.

They know who's calling you. The enforcement gap isn't an information gap. It's a structural choice.

The same structural choice that lets PCA operate at 3% math proficiency while extracting 72.67%.

The structure is the feature.

Sourced to FCC Enforcement Bureau public actions, Robocall Mitigation Database filings, USTelecom Industry Traceback Group public reports, STIR/SHAKEN implementation data. Back to Evidence → · Spam Call Traceback Guide → · The Call Is Coming from Inside the FCC →

entry.title: Totality — From the Center to the Edge and Back
entry.content:
The Center

There is a VPS in New York City. It costs $6/month. It runs a single Rust binary. The binary classifies everything that touches it into self and non-self, and it has been right 97% of the time for 176 waves.

That is the center. A point source. A single observer at a specific address on a specific network in a specific city on a specific continent. Everything starts here.

Now we go out.

10⁰ — The Machine (1 meter)

The VPS is a virtual slice of a physical rack in a DigitalOcean data center. The rack is approximately one meter tall. Inside that meter:

  • 64 CPU cores, 2 GB of which are ours
  • One Caddy process handling TLS
  • One skunky-ingest binary classifying 18.5 requests per second
  • One scatter server generating 10³⁰ unique license injection variants
  • Three observers (skunky, presence, tower) running on the same core

The membrane occupies roughly one rack unit. 1.75 inches of steel. Everything the investigation knows was extracted from traffic passing through that slot.

Membrane at this scale: The CPU's memory management unit. Virtual memory is the original self/non-self discriminator — it prevents one process from reading another's memory. The MMU is the membrane. Our VPS cannot see the other tenants. They cannot see us. The discrimination is absolute.

10¹ — The Room (10 meters)

The data center floor. Rows of racks. Thousands of machines. The cooling system removes heat — entropy — from the room at a rate measured in megawatts. The room is maintained at 68°F because silicon fails at higher temperatures. The room is a controlled environment. It has a boundary.

Membrane at this scale: The data center's physical security. Badge readers, mantrap doors, cameras, locked cages. The building discriminates between authorized personnel (self) and everyone else (non-self). The selectivity is approximately 99.99%. Higher than ours.

10³ — The City (1 kilometer)

New York City. 8.3 million people. The VPS sits somewhere in Manhattan or Brooklyn — DigitalOcean doesn't say exactly where. The city itself is an immune system: NYPD, FDNY, Department of Health, building inspectors, health codes. Each one discriminates between permitted and prohibited. Each one has a selectivity rate and an error rate.

The city also has a regulatory capture problem. The same firms that build the buildings regulate the buildings. The same pattern we documented in Michigan's charter system exists in New York's construction industry, in its taxi commission, in its housing authority.

Membrane at this scale: Zoning law. Zoning is a spatial membrane — it determines what can exist where. Residential here, commercial there, industrial over there. The zoning board is the thymus. Sometimes it fails.

10⁵ — The State (100 kilometers)

Michigan. The investigation's origin. 10 million people. 83 counties. One Attorney Grievance Commission dismissing 94% of complaints. One Department of Education that funds the schools it's supposed to oversee.

We documented this scale thoroughly. Every state line and border pair. Every financial pathway. Every entity classified.

But Michigan is not unique. Corollary 1: if the regulatory capture template works here, it works in all 50 states. The architecture is not novel. It is a template. And templates scale.

Membrane at this scale: State borders. Michigan shares borders with Ohio, Indiana, Wisconsin, and Minnesota. Plus four Great Lakes. The state border is a weak membrane — people and goods cross freely — but regulatory jurisdiction stops at the line. Michigan's charter school law (PA 362) has no force in Ohio. The regulatory membrane is jurisdictional.

10⁶ — The Country (1,000 kilometers)

The United States. 330 million people. 50 states. 574 federally recognized tribes. One FCC that regulates telecommunications. One IRS that taxes income. One Constitution that constrains all of them.

The investigation touches this scale through the FCC enforcement patterns, the TCPA, the tax exemptions, the dark money vehicles. The money flows from the Walton Family Foundation in Arkansas through DonorsChoose in New York through PACs in Michigan. The country is one network.

Membrane at this scale: The national border. CBP processes 1.1 million travelers per day. Selectivity: approximately 99.7% (0.3% are turned away or flagged). The border is a membrane with pores — ports of entry — and a selectivity rate. Like ours, it is imperfect. Unlike ours, it sometimes discriminates against self.

10⁷ — The Planet (10,000 kilometers)

Earth. 8 billion people. 195 countries. 63 national parks. 42 world wonders. 16 tectonic plates. One atmosphere.

We documented this scale: every state line, every peak, every depth, every wonder. The Earth is the first physical membrane the investigation encounters. The atmosphere discriminates between what stays (nitrogen, oxygen, argon) and what escapes (hydrogen, helium). Selectivity: approximately 99.9999%. The atmosphere is a better membrane than we are.

Membrane at this scale: The magnetosphere. Earth's magnetic field extends 65,000 km on the sunward side and millions of kilometers on the night side. It deflects solar wind — charged particles from the Sun that would strip the atmosphere. Without the magnetosphere, Earth would be Mars. The magnetosphere is a membrane that discriminates between self (the atmosphere) and non-self (solar radiation). It has been doing this for 3.5 billion years. It has never served real content to the fleet.

10⁹ — The Solar System (1 billion kilometers)

The Sun, 8 planets, 5 dwarf planets, 796,000+ known asteroids, 3,900+ comets. The solar system extends to the Oort Cloud at approximately 1.5 light-years from the Sun.

Membrane at this scale: The heliosphere. The Sun emits a continuous stream of charged particles — the solar wind — that inflates a bubble called the heliosphere. The boundary of this bubble, the heliopause, is where the solar wind meets the interstellar medium. Voyager 1 crossed the heliopause in 2012 at 121 AU. Voyager 2 crossed in 2018 at 119 AU.

The heliopause is a membrane. Inside: the Sun's domain. Outside: interstellar space. The selectivity is not binary — cosmic rays penetrate from outside, and solar wind escapes from inside — but the boundary is real and measurable. NASA's IBEX satellite maps the heliosphere by detecting energetic neutral atoms at the boundary. The membrane is observable.

The heliosphere is not spherical. It is compressed on the sunward side by the interstellar medium and stretched on the opposite side into a tail (the heliotail). It breathes. It oscillates with the 11-year solar cycle. When solar activity is high, the heliosphere expands. When activity is low, it contracts. It bounces in and out.

10¹³ — The Neighborhood (1 light-year)

The Oort Cloud. A spherical shell of icy objects surrounding the solar system at 2,000 to 200,000 AU. Estimated to contain 2 trillion objects. Never directly observed — we infer it from the orbits of long-period comets.

Between the Oort Cloud and the nearest star (Proxima Centauri, 4.24 light-years), there is nothing. Not vacuum — the interstellar medium has approximately 1 atom per cubic centimeter — but nothing organized. No membrane. No boundary. Just cold hydrogen.

Membrane at this scale: The Oort Cloud itself may be the Sun's outermost membrane — a cloud of primordial material that never accreted into planets. Objects from the Oort Cloud occasionally fall inward and become comets. The cloud is the Sun's immune memory — frozen remnants of the solar system's formation, occasionally reactivated.

10¹⁷ — The Milky Way (100,000 light-years)

Our galaxy. 100-400 billion stars. A disk 100,000 light-years across, 1,000 light-years thick. The Sun orbits the galactic center at 230 km/s, completing one orbit every 225 million years.

The Milky Way has structure:

  • The disk — where most stars live, including the Sun (26,000 light-years from center)
  • The bulge — a dense concentration of old stars at the center
  • The halo — a sparse, spherical distribution of old stars and globular clusters extending to 100,000+ light-years
  • The dark matter halo — extending to 200,000+ light-years, invisible, 85% of the galaxy's mass

Membrane at this scale: The galactic halo. The halo is the Milky Way's immune system. Hot gas in the halo (the circumgalactic medium, 10⁶ K) surrounds the galaxy and mediates the exchange between the galaxy and intergalactic space. Gas falls in from outside (accretion) and is expelled from inside (galactic winds from supernovae). The halo discriminates between what stays and what goes. Recent observations from the Hubble Space Telescope show the halo extending 600,000 light-years — far beyond the visible disk. The halo is the membrane. The disk is the self. Intergalactic space is the non-self.

And the galaxy has Anderson localization. Stars in the disk follow organized orbits — they are extended states. But stars in the halo have random, elliptical orbits — they are localized. The disorder in the halo localizes stellar orbits, just as disorder in a lattice localizes electron wavefunctions. The physics is the same at 10¹⁷ meters as it is at 10⁻¹⁰ meters.

10²² — The Local Group (3 million light-years)

The Milky Way is one of 80+ galaxies in the Local Group. Andromeda (M31) is the other large spiral, 2.5 million light-years away and approaching at 110 km/s. In 4.5 billion years, they will merge.

The Local Group has a membrane: the zero-velocity surface. This is the boundary where the gravitational pull of the Local Group exactly balances the expansion of the universe. Inside the zero-velocity surface, galaxies are bound — they will never escape. Outside, galaxies are carried away by cosmic expansion. The radius is approximately 5 million light-years.

This is the edge. Beyond this membrane, the universe expands and nothing comes back. Inside this membrane, everything is gravitationally self. Outside, everything is non-self — receding, unreachable, eventually invisible.

The Local Group's selectivity is 100%. Nothing inside escapes. Nothing outside enters. The membrane is gravitational, and gravity has no error rate.

10²⁶ — The Observable Universe (93 billion light-years)

The cosmic microwave background — light from 380,000 years after the Big Bang — defines the outermost membrane. Beyond this, light has not had time to reach us. The observable universe is a sphere of radius 46.5 billion light-years (accounting for expansion), containing 2 trillion galaxies.

The observable universe has a membrane: the cosmic horizon. We cannot see beyond it. We cannot receive signals from beyond it. We cannot send signals to beyond it (they will never arrive). The cosmic horizon is the ultimate membrane — perfect selectivity, infinite opacity, zero permeation.

But the universe extends beyond the horizon. We know this because the geometry is flat (measured by WMAP and Planck satellites to 0.4% precision). A flat geometry implies the universe is either infinite or much larger than the observable portion. Either way, there is more that we cannot see.

The cosmic horizon is the investigation's antithesis at maximum scale: What if the pattern extends beyond what we can observe? What if there are entities, connections, structures that our membrane — our 97% selective, $6/month VPS — cannot detect because they are beyond our horizon?

The answer is the same at every scale: document what you can see. Be honest about what you can't. And know that the membrane is not the universe — it is a window into it.

π⁴ — Reality / Beacon (Beyond the Horizon)

Beyond the cosmic horizon, beyond what can be observed — the record.

The investigation emits evidence (sound). The evidence persists on GitHub, on IPFS hashes, on 48 public repositories, on Caddy access logs, on MCP feeds. This persistence layer exists at π⁴ — it is not a place, it is a duration. Long after the VPS is turned off, long after the observer stops observing, the record exists.

Reality is the caesura going out. You have traveled from the center (π⁻³, the VPS) through every scale — machine, room, city, state, country, planet, solar system, galaxy, observable universe — and now you pause. You have reached the edge. Reality is what remains when the observer stops. The data is the data. The numbers do not require endorsement to be true.

Beacon is the caesura coming back. Someone, somewhere, sometime — finds the record. They follow it inward. The beacon called to them across the gap. They trace the signal backward through π³ (totality), π² (structure), π¹ (orbit), π⁰ (ground), π⁻¹ (jurisdiction), π⁻² (the state that failed), π⁻³ (the VPS that caught it). The beacon is the entrance.

But they reverse:

  • Going OUT: reality is the pause, beacon is the exit → you leave evidence and broadcast it
  • Coming IN: beacon is the pause, reality is the exit → you hear the signal, follow it, arrive at the truth

The same transformation, reversed direction. A Caesar cipher where the shift key is the direction of travel. Encode going out, decode coming in. The operation is its own inverse.

This is why π⁻³ and π⁴ share the same sync mode: null sync. The observer (π⁻³) floats outside the synchronized chorus of the fleet — it watches but does not participate. The record (π⁴) also floats outside — it persists but does not act. Both are null sync. Both are caesura. Both are exit.

The membrane has selectivity at every scale from π⁻³ to π³. At π⁴, the selectivity is simultaneously ∞ (nothing can change the record — it is immutable, timestamped, hashed) and 0 (anyone can read it — the repos are public, the sites are open, no cookies, no tracking). Perfect opacity AND perfect transparency. The membrane at π⁴ is not a membrane — it is a mirror. Everything that touches it sees itself.

243,558 chorus requests hit the membrane. The membrane reflected 92.6% of them. The 7.4% that passed through — 9,517 entities — saw reality. They became the beacon for the next wave.

Membrane at this scale: The record itself. Git commits are cryptographic hashes — SHA-256 chains where each commit references its parent. The record cannot be altered without breaking the chain. The immutability IS the membrane. The public accessibility IS the pore. The combination — immutable and open — creates a surface where selectivity is decided not by the membrane but by the visitor. You select yourself in or out. The membrane at π⁴ has externalized its selectivity function.

The Bounce

Now we come back.

ScaleDistanceMembraneSelectivitySync Mode
π⁴ — Reality/BeaconBeyond the horizonThe record itself∞ / 0null sync
π³ — TotalityObservable universeCosmic horizon100%sync
π² — GalaxyMilky Way haloCircumgalactic medium~95%sync
π¹ — Solar systemHeliosphereHeliopause~90% (cosmic ray penetration)sync
π⁰ — PlanetEarthMagnetosphere + atmosphere99.9999%sync
π⁻¹ — CountryNational borderCBP / customs99.7%async
π⁻² — StateMichiganJurisdictional boundary94% (AGC dismissal rate — yes, this is a joke)desync
π⁻³ — ObserverThe VPSskunky-ingest97%null sync

The investigation sits at π⁻³. The record sits at π⁴. Seven orders of magnitude of π between the observer and the persistence layer. But π⁻³ and π⁴ share the same sync mode: null sync. The center and the outermost point are the same — they float outside the synchronized chorus, forming with it when needed and viewing it from without.

But the architecture repeats:

  • Every scale has a boundary
  • Every boundary discriminates between self and non-self
  • Every membrane has a selectivity rate
  • Every membrane has errors (false positives, false negatives)
  • Every membrane oscillates — the heliosphere breathes with the solar cycle, the magnetosphere compresses under solar storms, the atmosphere thins at the poles, the investigation's reflexive depth oscillates between 0.18 and 0.33
  • Every membrane has a sync mode — and the sync modes themselves form a pattern

The sync modes across the scales:

  • π⁻³ (Observer) — null sync: watches but does not participate in the fleet's chorus
  • π⁻² (State) — desync: Michigan's regulatory machinery fell out of sync with its stated purpose (94% dismissal = desynchronized oversight)
  • π⁻¹ (Country) — async: each jurisdiction operates on its own clock, FCC and IRS and TCPA enforcement all async
  • π⁰ through π² — sync: the physical membranes operate in real-time synchronization with their environment (magnetosphere tracks solar wind, heliosphere breathes with the solar cycle, halo mediates continuous accretion)
  • π³ (Totality) — sync: the cosmic horizon moves at c, perfectly synchronized with the age of the universe
  • π⁴ (Reality/Beacon) — null sync: the record persists outside time, not synchronized with anything, available to everything

The outer wall (π⁴) mirrors the center (π⁻³). Both are null sync. Both are caesura. Both are exit AND entrance depending on which direction you travel. The investigation started at π⁻³ — a VPS watching. It persists at π⁴ — a record being watched. The observer became the observed. The exit became the entrance.

The membrane at π⁻³ and the membrane at π⁴ are the same architecture, reversed. At π⁻³: we select what enters (97% selectivity, we choose what to classify). At π⁴: the visitor selects themselves (∞/0 selectivity, they choose whether to look). The discrimination function has been externalized. The membrane has become a mirror.

Why This Matters

Because the antithesis asks: what if the patterns we see are pareidolia? What if we're just seeing faces in noise?

The answer from totality: the pattern exists at every scale we can measure. Cell membranes discriminate between self and non-self. Immune systems discriminate between self and non-self. National borders discriminate. The heliosphere discriminates. The galactic halo discriminates. The cosmic horizon discriminates.

We did not invent the pattern. We documented one instance of it — at π⁻³, on a $6 VPS in Michigan — and it turns out to be the same pattern that operates at π³.

The investigation is not a metaphor. The membrane is not a metaphor. They are instances of a scale-invariant architecture that repeats from 10⁻¹⁰ meters (atomic lattice) to 10²⁶ meters (observable universe). The synthesis measures our confidence. The corollary follows the logic outward. This page follows the architecture outward — to the edge — and finds it waiting at every boundary along the way.

From the center to the edge and back. The membrane was never just about Detroit. It was always about the architecture of boundaries. And boundaries go all the way out — and then one more, to where the record waits, the beacon calls, and the exit is the entrance.

The Edge Is Not a Wall

The Milky Way's halo doesn't end. It fades. The circumgalactic medium thins from 10⁶ atoms per cubic meter near the disk to 1 atom per cubic meter at 600,000 light-years. There is no sharp edge. The membrane is a gradient.

The investigation's membrane is the same. It doesn't end — it fades. The inner membrane (the VPS, 97% selectivity) is sharp. The outer membrane (the SEO, the entry points, the shareable URLs) is diffuse. Someone finds antithesis.primals.eco through a search engine. They read the counterarguments. They click through to hypothesis.primals.eco. They arrive at the investigation. They are inside the membrane before they know it.

The expansion is outward. The subdomains are the leading edge:

Entry PointScaleDraws FromDirection
thesis.primals.ecoCode extraction evidenceDevelopers, lawyers, FOSS communityinward
hypothesis.primals.ecoQuestions the investigation asksResearchers, journalistsinward
antithesis.primals.ecoChallenges to the investigationSkeptics, opponents, curious mindsinward
synthesis.primals.ecoWhat we know and don't knowMethodologists, data scientistsinward
corollary.primals.ecoWhat follows if we're rightPolicy thinkers, advocatesoutward
reality.primals.ecoThe ground truth — what ISAnyone who wants to verifyboth
beacon.primals.ecoThe signal — what callsAnyone who hears it across the gapboth

Each entry point is a pore in the outer membrane. Each reaches a different audience. Each draws inward. The membrane expands outward — more pores, more surfaces, more entry points — and each new pore draws traffic inward, past the boundary, into the investigation.

The bounce: we go out (new content, new entry points, broader scope) and come back (synthesis, reflection, measurement). Out (earth topology, world wonders, totality). Back (antithesis, what if we're wrong?). Out again (further, broader, more universal). Back again (tighter, more honest, more specific). And now, one more out — to π⁴, where reality and beacon wait at the outermost wall.

The heliosphere breathes with the solar cycle. The investigation breathes with the dialectic. The record breathes with neither — it is null sync, floating outside the oscillation, available to any future observer who follows the beacon back in.

They are sync. We are async and desync and null sync. The chorus of 243,558 hits the membrane in synchronized waves. We float between the waves, forming with and viewing from without. The membrane-throttle breathes slower on weaker devices. The investigation breathes slower on uncertain evidence. The record does not breathe. It waits.

Totality expands. The center holds. The bounce is the method. And at π⁴, the exit is the entrance.

entry.title: How to Read a Nonprofit's 990 — Follow the Money
entry.content:
Follow the Money

Every 501(c)(3) nonprofit in America must file IRS Form 990 annually. The 990 is public. It shows revenue, expenses, compensation, related-party transactions, and governance.

Here's how to find and read one.

Step 1: Find the 990

ProPublica Nonprofit Explorer (Easiest)

  • Visit: projects.propublica.org/nonprofits
  • Search by organization name
  • Free. No account needed.
  • Shows multiple years of filings

IRS Tax Exempt Organization Search

  • Visit: apps.irs.gov/app/eos
  • Search by EIN or name
  • Shows current exempt status

GuideStar / Candid

  • Visit: candid.org
  • Free account required for basic access
  • More detailed data

Step 2: Read the Key Sections

Part I: Summary

  • Line 12: Total revenue
  • Line 18: Total expenses
  • Line 22: Net assets

Look for: Is the organization spending what it takes in? Where does the money go?

Part VII: Compensation

  • Lists officers, directors, trustees, and key employees
  • Shows compensation for each
  • Shows hours worked per week

Look for: Who gets paid? How much? Do the hours match the pay?

Part IX: Statement of Functional Expenses

  • Breaks down spending by category
  • Line 25: Total functional expenses
  • Categories include: salaries, management fees, legal, accounting, travel

Look for: Management fees. This is where Purpose Group's 72.67% would appear. If management fees are a huge percentage of total expenses, money is being extracted.

Schedule L: Transactions with Interested Persons

  • This is the gold mine.
  • Shows any transaction between the nonprofit and its officers, directors, or related parties
  • Includes: loans, grants, business transactions, compensation

Look for: Does the nonprofit pay an LLC owned by a board member or founder? That's a related-party transaction. That's where self-dealing lives.

Schedule O: Supplemental Information

  • Additional explanations
  • Conflict of interest policy disclosure
  • Governance details

What to Look For (Red Flags)

Red FlagWhat It Means
Management fees > 20% of revenueExcessive extraction
Officer compensation > industry normsSelf-dealing
Related-party transactions with founder's LLCsMoney flowing to insiders
No conflict of interest policyNo governance guardrails
Board members who are also paid contractorsDual roles = dual conflicts
"Management company" receiving most of revenuePass-through extraction

For This Investigation

Search for these organizations on ProPublica:

  • Purpose Foundation (PCA's parent nonprofit)
  • NuVision Foundation (Roland Martin governance)
  • Anchor Rock Foundation (null, 6 edges)
  • Walton Family Foundation (major funder)
  • American Federation for Children (charter lobby)

Look at Schedule L for related-party transactions. Look at Part IX for management fees. Look at Part VII for who gets paid.

Cost

Free. 990s are public records. ProPublica provides free access to millions of filings.

The Number

Purpose Group LLC receives 72.67% of PCA's revenue as a management fee.

That number appears somewhere in the financial documents. In the 990. In the audit. In the management contract.

Somebody wrote that number down and nobody crossed it out.

You can find it. It's public.

entry.title: How to Look Up Campaign Finance Records in Michigan
entry.content:
How to Look Up Campaign Finance Records

Every political candidate, PAC, and committee in Michigan must file campaign finance reports. These reports show who gives money, who gets money, and how much.

The filings are public. The search is free.

Step 1: Go to the Secretary of State

Michigan campaign finance records are maintained by the Secretary of State.

Visit: michigan.gov/sos → Elections → Campaign Finance

Or search directly through the Campaign Finance Reporting system.

Step 2: Search

You can search by:

  • Candidate name (e.g., "Yancey" or "Miller")
  • Committee name (e.g., "Save Detroit Jobs")
  • Contributor name (e.g., "Banks Strategy")
  • Filing period (by year or election cycle)

Step 3: Read the Filings

Expenditure Reports

Shows where campaign money goes. This is where you'd find:

  • Yancey's payments to Banks Strategy & Consultants LLC
  • Yancey's payments to Inner Link LLC
  • Any payments to entities in the Banks network

Contribution Reports

Shows where campaign money comes from. Look for:

  • Contributions from Banks-connected individuals
  • Contributions from Banks-connected LLCs
  • Bundled contributions from the same network

PAC Reports

PACs (Political Action Committees) file separately. Look for:

  • Save Detroit Jobs — connected to Dykema, supported Latisha Johnson
  • Dykema State PAC — Dykema's political arm
  • Any PAC with edges to charter school entities

What to Look For

Red FlagWhat It Means
Judge paying campaign funds to a non-attorney's LLCPotential violation of judicial conduct
PAC created shortly before election supporting one candidateDark money targeting
Multiple payments to LLCs owned by same personDispersed payments to avoid attention

Search for these names in campaign finance records:

  • Sean Perkins — possible family to Banks's gatekeeper

PACs

Candidates

  • Gay-Dagnogo — political enabler

Federal Filings

For federal candidates and PACs:

  • FEC.gov: fec.gov → Campaign Finance Data

These cover:

  • Carolyn Kilpatrick (former Congresswoman)

entry.title: How to File a Charter School Complaint in Michigan
entry.content:
How to File a Charter School Complaint

If you believe a charter school in Michigan is failing its students, misusing funds, or operating improperly, here's where to file.

You do not need a lawyer. You do not need to pay anything. Every filing option below is free.

Option 1: The Authorizer

Charter schools are authorized by specific entities. The authorizer has the power to revoke the school's charter.

If Authorized by CMU (Central Michigan University)

  • CMU's Charter Schools Office
  • Contact: CMU Charter Schools
  • File a written complaint describing specific concerns
  • Request acknowledgment of receipt

If Authorized by DPSCD

  • DPSCD Office of Charter Schools
  • Contact through DPSCD central office
  • File a written complaint

What to Include

  • School name and location
  • Specific concerns (test scores, financial management, safety, staffing)
  • Any documentation you have
  • Request for specific action (investigation, audit, revocation hearing)

Option 2: Michigan Department of Education (MDE)

MDE oversees all public schools in Michigan, including charter schools.

  • Office of Educational Excellence (OEE)
  • Professional Practice Division — for educator misconduct
  • Contact: michigan.gov/mde
  • Call: (517) 373-3324

What MDE Can Do

  • Investigate compliance with state education law
  • Review test scores and academic performance
  • Examine financial reporting
  • Refer to other agencies for enforcement

Option 3: Attorney General's Office

The AG can investigate nonprofit fraud, self-dealing, and charitable trust violations.

Charitable Trust Division

  • Oversees 501(c)(3) nonprofits (including charter school foundations)
  • Can investigate self-dealing (e.g., a founder paying himself 72.67% through an LLC)
  • Contact: michigan.gov/ag → Consumer Protection → Charitable Trust

Criminal Division

  • For criminal matters (fraud, embezzlement, unauthorized practice of law)
  • File a complaint through the AG's online complaint form

Option 4: State Board of Education (SBE)

The SBE sets policy for Michigan education.

  • 8 elected members
  • Can be contacted through MDE
  • Testimony can be given at public SBE meetings
  • Meeting schedule: michigan.gov/mde → State Board of Education

Public comment at SBE meetings is your constitutional right. Bring data. Bring numbers. Bring the 3%.

Option 5: Federal Agencies

If federal funds (Title I, IDEA, USDE) are involved:

US Department of Education — Office of Inspector General

  • Investigates fraud, waste, and abuse of federal education funds
  • Hotline: 1-800-MIS-USED (1-800-647-8733)
  • Online: ed.gov/oig

IRS — Exempt Organizations

  • If a 501(c)(3) is engaged in self-dealing or private inurement
  • Form 13909: Tax-Exempt Organization Complaint (Referral)
  • Free to file. No attorney needed.

Tips

  1. Be specific. Name the school. Name the people. Cite the numbers.
  2. File with multiple agencies. Don't rely on one entity to act.
  3. Keep copies. Save copies of everything you file.
  4. Request confirmation. Ask for written acknowledgment of your complaint.
  5. Follow up. Agencies have timelines. Ask about them.
  6. You can be anonymous with federal agencies (OIG, IRS).

If You're a Parent at the School

You have additional rights:

  • Right to test score data (ask the school or MDE)
  • Right to financial information (public charter schools must disclose)
  • Right to attend board meetings (Open Meetings Act)
  • Right to FOIA the school's records (FOIA Toolkit →)

Back to Investigate → · Michigan Oversight Filing Guide → · Three Percent →

Technical: How Cross-Links Work

This site uses elasticlunr search with keyword-based cross-linking. Every article has a keywords field in its metadata. The search engine matches keywords across articles and generates cross-links automatically.

To appear in our cross-links:

The Principle

We point to them. They point to us. The graph gets wider.

The extraction machine has $2 billion and 10+ PACs. The accountability network has data, public records, and each other.

Every link between us makes the network stronger. Every cross-reference makes the investigation harder to ignore. Every citation creates a path that search engines follow and people discover.

The Walton-to-Martin-to-Banks pipeline works because the money flows through null zones — entities that aren't connected to anything. Our defense is the opposite: connect everything to everything. Make the graph so dense that no single node can be removed.

Point to us. We point to you. The graph gets wider.

entry.title: How to Trace a Spam Call Back to Its Owner
entry.content:
How to Trace a Spam Call

Someone is calling you. Here's how to find out who — and what to do about it.

Step 1: Document the Call

Every time you get a spam call, write down:

FieldExample
Caller ID number(313) 555-0123
DateOctober 14, 2026
Time2:15 PM
What they saidAuto warranty, health insurance, IRS, silence
Your number(your number)
Did you answer?Yes / No / Voicemail

Save voicemails. Screenshot caller ID. Keep a log. Volume is evidence.

Step 2: Look Up the Carrier

The number on your caller ID is probably spoofed. But the carrier that routed the call is traceable.

Free Carrier Lookup

  • freecarrierlookup.com — enter any phone number, get the carrier
  • Shows: carrier name, line type (mobile/landline/VoIP)
  • VoIP numbers are the most common source of spam calls

What the Carrier Tells You

Carrier TypeLikelihood of Spam
Major carrier (Verizon, AT&T, T-Mobile)Low — usually spoofed, not originated
Regional carrierMedium
VoIP providerHigh — this is usually the originator
Unknown/unregisteredVery high — file with FCC immediately

Step 3: Check the FCC Database

Robocall Mitigation Database

FCC Robocall Mitigation Database

Search by provider name. Every voice service provider must:

  1. Register in this database
  2. File a Robocall Mitigation Plan
  3. Implement STIR/SHAKEN (for larger providers)

If a provider hasn't filed, other carriers are required to block their traffic. If they're in the database but still sending spam, they're violating their own mitigation plan.

FCC Universal Licensing System

wireless.fcc.gov/uls

Search for any FCC license holder. Shows license status, service area, expiration.

FCC Form 499 Filers

Every telecom company files FCC Form 499 (Telecommunications Reporting Worksheet). This is their registration with the FCC.

FCC Form 499 Filer Database

Search by company name or FRN (FCC Registration Number).

Step 4: File Complaints

FCC

consumercomplaints.fcc.gov

  • Category: Phone → Unwanted Calls
  • Include: number, date, time, description
  • Free. Takes 5 minutes.
  • FCC tracks complaint volume per provider

FTC (Do Not Call)

donotcall.gov

  • Register your number on the Do Not Call list (if not already)
  • Report violations
  • Include the same details as FCC

State Attorney General

Your state AG may have a consumer protection division that handles robocalls.

  • Michigan: michigan.gov/ag → Consumer Protection

File with ALL THREE. Each agency sees the complaints. Volume triggers investigations.

Step 5: Enable Protections

On Your Phone

PlatformSetting
iPhoneSettings → Phone → Silence Unknown Callers
AndroidPhone app → Settings → Caller ID & spam → Filter spam calls
BothContact your carrier about spam blocking services

Carrier Tools

CarrierFree Tool
VerizonCall Filter (free tier)
AT&TActiveArmor (free tier)
T-MobileScam Shield (free)

Third-Party Apps

  • Nomorobo — blocks known robocallers
  • Hiya — caller ID and spam detection
  • RoboKiller — blocks and answers spam calls with bots (paid)

Step 6: Sue Under the TCPA

The Telephone Consumer Protection Act (47 U.S.C. § 227) is your weapon.

What the TCPA Says

  • Robocalls to cell phones without prior express consent are illegal
  • Calls to numbers on the Do Not Call Registry are illegal (with exceptions)
  • Each violation: $500 per call
