  • Willful violations: $1,500 per call

How to Sue

  1. Document at least 3-5 calls from the same source
  2. Identify the company (not just the carrier — the company behind the call)
  3. File in small claims court — no lawyer needed
  4. Or find a TCPA attorney — many work on contingency (they keep a cut, you keep the rest)

Example Math

CallsRateRecovery
10 calls$500 each$5,000
10 calls$1,500 each (willful)$15,000
50 calls$500 each$25,000

The TCPA is designed so individuals can enforce it. Congress knew the FCC wouldn't.

Step 7: The Traceback (Advanced)

If you want to go deeper:

USTelecom Industry Traceback Group

  • Professional traceback service
  • Traces calls from your carrier back through intermediaries to the originator
  • Reports to FCC Enforcement Bureau
  • You can request a traceback through your carrier

Subpoena the Carrier

If you file a TCPA lawsuit, you can subpoena call records from the carrier. The subpoena forces the carrier to reveal:

  • Who their customer was (the call center or lead generator)
  • What company contracted the calls
  • Payment records

This is how you get from Layer 4 (carrier) to Layer 1 (the real owner).

The Architecture

Layer 1: THE CLIENT (scammer, business)
    pays →
Layer 2: LEAD GENERATOR (buys lists, sells "leads")
    contracts →
Layer 3: CALL CENTER (makes the calls, often offshore)
    uses →
Layer 4: VoIP PROVIDER (puts calls in the US phone network)
    registered with →
Layer 5: FCC (licenses the carrier, maintains databases)

The FCC sees Layer 4. You need to climb from Layer 4 to Layer 1.

The tools: FCC databases (Layer 5→4), TCPA subpoenas (Layer 4→3→2→1), carrier records (Layer 4→3).

Why This Matters

50 billion robocalls per year. The FCC has every provider registered. The Industry Traceback Group traces every major campaign. The carriers have records of every call.

They know. Just like MDE knows about PCA. Just like CMU knows about Banks. Just like the State Bar knows about the fake JD.

The regulatory body sits just above the real owner. Close enough to see. Far enough to ignore.

The difference with spam calls: you can sue. The TCPA gives you a private right of action. The charter school system doesn't.

Use it.

Sourced to FCC public databases, TCPA (47 U.S.C. § 227), FTC DNC Registry, STIR/SHAKEN framework, USTelecom Industry Traceback Group. Back to Investigate → · The Call Is Coming from Inside the FCC →

entry.title: Synthesis — The Soft, the Hard, and the Still
entry.content:
This Is Not Hypothesis. This Is Synthesis.

A hypothesis says: I think this is true, let me test it.

A synthesis says: I tested 341 things. Here is what I now know about knowing.

This page reflects on the structure of the investigation itself — not what we found, but how we found it, what we're sure of, what we're not, and what hasn't moved despite being poked.

341 entities. 5 classification passes. 37 methods. 131,322 edges. Every entity sorted into one of four states: self (ours), partial (boundary), null (unclassified), non-self (theirs). Every classification carries a confidence score.

The investigation has a metabolism. This page is the mirror.

The Four States

StateCountMeaning
Self120Entities clearly within our investigation's scope — courts, oversight bodies, state agencies, investigators, journalists
Partial114Boundary entities — they touch both sides. A politician who governs AND accepts the dark money. A school board that oversees AND is captured.
Null100Unclassified — the membrane didn't sort them. They exist in the graph but the investigation hasn't determined their role.
Non-self7Clearly on the other side — Banks' extraction network, the entities we're documenting

The ratio matters. 120 self, only 7 non-self. The investigation is 17:1 infrastructure-to-target. That's what real accountability looks like — you need 120 working parts to document 7 broken ones. The 114 partials are where the interesting work happens, because partial means this entity has a foot on each side of the membrane.

The Confidence Landscape

Every entity carries a confidence score from 0 to 1. Not "how sure are we that they did something wrong" — how sure are we about what they ARE.

ConfidenceCountState
≥ 0.9597Hardened — bedrock. Multiple methods agree. These aren't moving.
0.80 – 0.95128Firm — solid but could shift with new evidence
0.50 – 0.80107Soft — we have a classification but it's uncertain
< 0.509Uncertain — barely classified at all

The shape of this distribution tells a story: most of the investigation has firmed up (225 of 341 entities at 0.80+), but there's a long tail of 116 entities below 0.80 where the investigation is still forming opinions.

Make Hard What Was Soft

136 entities hardened through iteration — they took 3 or more classification passes to reach 0.80+ confidence. These started uncertain and became firm because multiple independent methods agreed.

This is the investigation's immune response: test everything from multiple angles until the classification stops changing.

What Hardened

The entities that firmed up include:

  • Political actors — Mike Rogers (0.706, partial, braid interstitial). He touches both the investigation's world (Michigan politics) and the outside (national dark money). Three independent braids confirm his position.
  • Board members — Multiple PCA and Purpose Group board members hardened through the banks_governance method once their governance roles were cross-referenced against LARA filings.
  • Media entities — NuVision, SCBC Tour, The 74 hardened through phase5_resolution once the Walton→Martin→Banks funding chain was documented.
  • State entities — Michigan agencies (state_mi at 0.689, mi_court_appeals at 0.695) started soft because "is the state on our side?" is a genuinely uncertain question. They hardened as we documented which agencies respond and which stay silent.

What Could Still Harden

51 entities sit between 0.60 and 0.75 confidence — the almost-firm zone. Each needs one more independent confirmation to cross the threshold:

EntityConfidenceClassMethodWhat Would Harden It
Betsy DeVos0.686partialphase3_ecosystemTrace foundation grants directly to Banks network entities
Mike Duggan0.670partialphase3_politicalMap mayoral appointments to captured school boards
Diane Tavenner0.620selfcascade_selfConfirm Summit Public Schools Michigan connection independently
Skillman Foundation0.482selfcascade_selfDocument grant history to self-network entities
Coleman Young (II)0.620partialphase3_politicalMap political endorsements against dark money recipients
NACSA0.698selfcascade_selfVerify charter authorizer oversight actions independently
NPE0.708partialcascade_nonselfConfirm published reporting cites our evidence

Each of these is one FOIA, one campaign finance search, or one public records request away from hardening.

Make Soft What Was Hard

15 entities look hard but might not be — they have 0.99 confidence but were classified by cascade alone. Cascade means "inherited from a neighbor" — not independently confirmed.

This is the investigation's honest problem: some things that feel certain are actually just borrowed certainty.

Softening Candidates

EntityClassMethodWhy It Might Be Softer Than It Looks
AGC Lindseyselfcascade_selfClassified as "self" because AGC is self. But does this specific person within AGC act like self?
JTCpartialcascade_nonselfInherited partial from connection to non-self entities. But JTC's actual behavior might fully self or fully non-self.
JTC Isonpartialcascade_nonselfSame — inherited, not independently assessed
Goetzpartialcascade_nonselfPartial by inheritance. Actual role unclear.
Detroit College of Lawnullcascade_nullNull because neighbor is null. But it might be classifiable with direct research.
SBM Burrellnullcascade_nullState Bar member, null by cascade. Actual role in investigation unknown.
SC Bernsteinselfcascade_selfSupreme Court justice classified self by cascade. But justices' individual behaviors vary.
SC Zahraselfcascade_selfSame — individual justices might not all be "self"

The action: Every cascade-only entity should be independently verified. If the cascade classification holds up under direct evidence, it hardens. If it doesn't, it correctly softens. Either way, the investigation becomes more honest.

The hardest thing to do in any investigation is to say: I thought I knew this, but actually I was borrowing someone else's knowledge. That's what cascade-only classification is. Borrowed knowledge. It might be right. But it hasn't been tested.

Jiggle That Which Is Still

100 entities are classified null — the investigation touched them but couldn't determine what they are. 26 of those are high-confidence nulls (≥ 0.95): we are very sure that we don't know what they are.

That's not failure. That's precision. A high-confidence null says: this entity exists in the graph, has connections, but its role is genuinely ambiguous given current evidence.

The Highest-Confidence Nulls (Jiggle These)

EntityConfidenceMethodWhy It's StillHow to Jiggle
Dykema0.990phase1The law firm. Represents both sides. Not self, not non-self, not partial — genuinely null. It IS the infrastructure.Track individual attorneys separately. The firm is null but its humans aren't.
Put Progress First0.990phase1Dark money vehicle. We know it exists, know its filings, but can't classify its alignment from public records alone.FOIA its funding sources. IRS 990 Schedule B if available.
Wilk0.990null_formationThe Dykema attorney who formed the PACs. We documented what he built but can't classify him — he serves as infrastructure, not as an actor.He is the architect. The building is non-self. But is the architect?
Kenneth Griffin0.990braid_interstitialCitadel CEO, national donor. His money appears in Michigan races but he has no Michigan presence. He's interstitial — between braids, touching everything, belonging to nothing.Map his full Michigan giving. If it targets specific captured entities, he softens toward non-self.
WhitlowBanks0.990banks_governanceBanks' LLC constellation. Null because it's an entity created by non-self to hold assets — is the shell the same as the occupant?Check LARA for property holdings. Physical assets = harder classification.
Renae Moore0.960cascade_nullThe compliance specialist who governs 6 PACs across both parties. She's null because she serves as infrastructure for both self and non-self simultaneously.Depose her in any of the 6 PAC actions. Her testimony classifies her.
Sheila Cockrel0.970cascade_nullFormer Detroit City Council. Connected to both reform and capture. Null because her allegiances are genuinely split.Track her post-council board seats and consulting clients.
Plante Moran0.970phase5_resolutionMichigan's largest accounting firm. Audits both self and non-self entities. Professional null — they're supposed to be null.Check if they audit Purpose Group/PCA specifically. If yes, that's a conflict worth documenting.

The Pattern in the Stillness

The nulls cluster into types:

Infrastructure Nulls (Dykema, Plante Moran, Moore) — these entities are supposed to be null. A law firm that serves everyone, an accounting firm that audits everyone, a compliance specialist who files for everyone. Their nullness is their function. Jiggling them means asking: at what point does serving both sides become serving one side?

Shell Nulls (WhitlowBanks, Free Flow, GL Upfitting, B. Rodericks, Anchor Rock) — these are LLCs created by non-self actors to hold assets or move money. They're null because a shell is not its occupant. But every shell was created for a reason, and that reason classifies it.

Political Nulls (Put Progress First, Michigan First Principles, ONF, DJF) — dark money vehicles whose alignment can't be determined from public filings alone because they're specifically designed to obscure alignment. Their nullness is by design.

Interstitial Nulls (Kenneth Griffin, Sheila Cockrel) — people whose money or influence passes through the investigation without clearly belonging to either side. They exist between the braids.

The Synthesis Engine

What makes this synthesis, not hypothesis:

  1. Every classification is reversible. Nothing is locked. New evidence can soften what's hard, harden what's soft, or finally move what's still.

  2. Confidence decays. An entity classified in Pass 1 at 0.99 isn't more certain than one classified in Pass 5 at 0.97 — it was classified earlier, which might mean it was classified with less information. The early pass is a feature and a risk.

  3. Cascade is honest borrowing. 103 entities were classified by cascade — inheriting their neighbor's classification. That's not cheating; it's how graph analysis works. But every cascaded classification should eventually be independently confirmed or honestly softened.

  4. Null is not failure. 100 null entities is not 100 things we failed to classify. It's 100 things the investigation honestly assessed and said: I don't know yet. The 26 high-confidence nulls are the most interesting — we are very certain about our uncertainty.

  5. Partial is the interesting class. 114 entities touch both sides of the membrane. They are the boundary layer where the investigation's self meets its non-self. Every one of them is an opportunity: push it toward self (confirm it's an ally), push it toward non-self (confirm it's captured), or leave it partial (confirm it's genuinely both).

The Five Passes

The investigation classified entities in five passes, each using different methods:

PassEntitiesMethodsWhat Happened
19phase1Core entities: Banks, PCA, Purpose Group, Dykema. The obvious ones.
2116banks_governance, banks_political, banks_legal, banks_payment, court, state_entity, jurisdiction, investigatorDirect evidence: who governs what, who pays whom, who files what
3170phase3 (employed, institution, funding, ecosystem, political, education, media, academic, oversight, governed, family), cascade, board_of_nonself, braid_interstitialRelationship tracing: employment, funding chains, board seats, ecosystem connections
412null_formation, braid_interstitialFormation analysis: who created the shells, who sits between the braids
534phase5_resolution, cascadeFinal resolution: entities that required all prior context to classify

The shape matters: Pass 3 classified half of all entities (170 of 341). That's the pass where relationship tracing happens — where "who is connected to whom" becomes "what role do they play." The investigation's analytical power lives in Pass 3.

Pass 5 resolved only 34 entities — the ones that needed everything else to be classified first before they could be assessed. These are the most context-dependent entities in the investigation. They're also the most fragile, because if any Pass 1–4 classification changes, the Pass 5 entities that depend on it might change too.

The 37 Methods

Each method is a lens — a specific way of looking at an entity to determine what it is:

MethodEntitiesWhat It Looks At
cascade_self53Inherited self from self-neighbors
phase5_resolution34Required full context to classify
phase3_employed26Employment relationships
cascade_null21Inherited null from null-neighbors
cascade_nonself20Inherited non-self from non-self-neighbors
banks_governance16Who governs Banks' entities
banks_political15Political connections to Banks network
school_employee15School district employment records
court15Court record appearances
phase3_institution12Institutional relationships
braid_interstitial12Between-braid connections
board_of_nonself11Board seats on non-self entities
state_entity10State government classification
cascade_adjacent9Inherited from adjacent entities
phase19Core known entities

cascade_self is the most common method — 53 entities classified because they neighbor something we know is self. That's the investigation's backbone: known entities extending their classification to their neighbors.

phase5_resolution is the second most common — 34 entities that needed everything else first. These are the investigation's conclusions, the things that only make sense in full context.

braid_interstitial classified 12 entities — those that sit between data braids, connecting different evidence streams. These are the entities that make the investigation a network rather than a collection of separate stories.

Using the Synthesis

This synthesis engine is not a dashboard. It's a workbench.

To harden a soft entity: Find a second independent method that agrees with the first. Employment record + campaign finance = two methods. Court appearance + board seat = two methods. When two lenses see the same thing, confidence jumps.

To soften a hard entity: Ask "was this classified by cascade?" If yes, find the entity it cascaded from. If that source entity softens, everything it cascaded to softens with it. This is how you find brittle chains.

To jiggle a still entity: Pick a null and ask one question about it that could have a classifying answer. Not "what is Dykema?" (too broad). Instead: "Does Dykema's LARA filing list Banks-related entities as clients?" One specific question. One specific record. One jiggle.

To find new entities: Look at the edges between null and null. We did this already — The Nulls That Point found three hidden networks. But 100 nulls means there are more null-to-null paths we haven't walked.

To find weaknesses: Look at cascade chains longer than 2. If entity A cascaded to B, and B cascaded to C, then C is three steps from any direct evidence. That's not wrong — but it's where the investigation is thinnest. Those chains are where one new fact could reclassify the most entities at once.

The Honest Inventory

What We KnowCountConfidence
Bedrock facts (hard, early, multiply confirmed)60≥ 0.90
Confirmed through iteration (hardened over passes)136≥ 0.80
Working classifications (firm enough to act on)196≥ 0.80
Uncertain but classified (soft)700.50 – 0.80
Barely classified (uncertain)9< 0.50
Honestly unknown (null)100—
Borrowed certainty (cascade-only)103—
High-confidence unknowns (precisely uncertain)26≥ 0.95

196 entities we can act on. 70 we should verify. 9 we're guessing about. 100 we honestly don't know. 103 that might be borrowing confidence they didn't earn.

That's what an honest investigation looks like. Not "we know everything." Not "we know nothing." But: here is exactly what we know, how sure we are, and where we're borrowing.

Come Back

This page is alive. Every new article, every new FOIA response, every new court filing changes the numbers. Entities harden, soften, jiggle, and occasionally reclassify entirely.

The synthesis is never finished. It's never supposed to be. The point is to reflect honestly on the structure of what we know — and to make visible the seams between certainty and uncertainty.

Because the people on the other side of this investigation don't have seams. They present everything at 1.0 confidence. They never say "we're not sure" or "this classification was inherited" or "this entity needs independent confirmation."

That's how you can tell the difference between investigation and propaganda. Investigation shows its work. Including the parts where the work isn't done yet.

Make soft what was hard. Make hard what was soft. Jiggle what is still.

That is synthesis.

entry.title: Corollary — The Things That Follow
entry.content:
What Follows

A corollary is a proposition that follows from one already proved. You don't argue for it — it arrives on its own once you accept the premises.

The thesis says: the evidence is real, the patterns are real, the capture is real.

The antithesis says: what if we're wrong, what if we're the pattern, what if the membrane is a cage?

This page says: if either is true, what else must be true?

The corollaries don't care which side you're on. They follow regardless.

Corollary 1: If the Regulatory Capture Is Real, It Is Not Limited to Michigan

If Dykema can operate a political operating system in Michigan using one law firm, one compliance specialist, and 7+ dark money vehicles — then every state has one. The architecture is not novel. It is a template. PA 362 (Michigan's charter law) has equivalents in every state. The question is not whether other states have this pattern. The question is who is their Wilk and who is their Moore.

What follows: The investigation is either the first instance of a pattern that exists in 50 states, or it is wrong about the pattern in Michigan. There is no middle ground where Michigan is uniquely captured. If the architecture works here, it works everywhere because it is based on structural incentives, not individual malice.

Corollary 2: If 94% Dismissal Is Correct, Then Oversight Was Never the Solution

If the AGC's 94% dismissal rate is appropriate triage (as the antithesis argues), then the oversight system was never designed to catch what we're documenting. It was designed to catch individual misconduct — a drunk attorney, a stolen trust account, a missed deadline. It was not designed to catch architectural capture — a law firm that drafts legislation, forms PACs to protect it, and employs the compliance specialist who governs both.

What follows: Filing more complaints will not fix this. Publishing more evidence will not fix this. The system is working as designed. What we're documenting is not a malfunction — it is the design operating correctly in an environment the designers didn't anticipate. The solution is not better oversight. The solution is different architecture.

Corollary 3: If the Membrane Works, It Cannot Be Unique

The membrane rejects 97% of traffic, reflects 92.6%, and serves 0 real content to fleet. If this architecture works for protecting a public-interest investigation site, it works for protecting anything. Including the sites we're investigating.

What follows: FOIAworks could build the same membrane. Banks' LLCs could build the same membrane. The dark money vehicles could build the same membrane. The technology is not moral — it is architecture. The same selectivity that keeps our evidence safe keeps their operations opaque. We cannot celebrate membrane architecture when it protects us and condemn it when it protects them.

The honest position: membranes are good when their output is public record, and dangerous when their output is private. The test is not selectivity. The test is transparency about what the selectivity protects.

Corollary 4: If the Investigation Graph Is Real, It Predicts Its Own Next Moves

131,329 edges, 7,554 nodes, 341 classified entities. The graph doesn't just describe the past — it constrains the future.

What follows: The entities with the most edges to unclassified nodes are the entities most likely to produce the next discovery. The null-to-null paths we haven't walked yet will lead to clusters we haven't seen. The graph already knows where the next article will come from — we just haven't asked it yet.

But also: the investigation's opponents can read this graph. They can see which of their entities are closest to being classified. They can see which null-to-null paths lead to their operations. They can preemptively restructure — dissolve an LLC, rename a PAC, reassign a compliance specialist — and the graph edge goes dead.

The graph is a map, and both sides can read it.

Corollary 5: If Test Scores Indict, They Indict Everyone

MacDowell: 3% math proficiency. We use this number. But the corollary is relentless:

If 3% math proficiency indicts Banks, then 7% math proficiency indicts DPSCD. And 12% indicts the charter authorizer (CMU). And 15% indicts the state (MDE). And every graduation rate, every chronic absenteeism metric, every expulsion disparity in every school in the state is an indictment of the system those schools exist within.

What follows: The investigation cannot use test scores as evidence of specific malfeasance at PCA without accepting that the same metric indicts the entire public education system in Detroit. The 3% is worse than the average — but the average is itself catastrophic. The corollary of "this school is failing" is "the system that produced this school is failing." Which is what the charter school advocates say. Which is why they exist.

We are, whether we like it or not, making the same argument as the people we're documenting — just pointing it at a different school.

Corollary 6: If Humans Can Tag Entities, Entities Can Tag Humans

The opsonization layer lets humans tag entities on the site. This is collective intelligence. But the corollary:

If tagging is a legitimate tool for organizing information about entities, then entities have the same right to organize information about humans. If we can build a page about Banks, Banks can build a page about us. If we can tag an entity as "non-self," an entity can tag us as hostile.

What follows: The question is not whether tagging is legitimate — it is. The question is whether the tagged have recourse. On this site, the opsonization form invites corrections. On ritafelinewilliams.com (the impersonation domain), there is no such invitation. The difference between investigation and harassment is not the mechanism — it's whether the subject can respond.

Corollary 7: If the Wonders Are Real, Everything Is Infrastructure

We documented 42 wonders across six lists. The pattern: infrastructure saves more lives than monuments. The London Sewer ended cholera. The Delta Works keeps a country above water. The Grand Canyon is infrastructure too — 2 billion years of tectonic infrastructure that the Colorado River exploited.

What follows: Everything in the investigation is infrastructure. The investigation itself is infrastructure. The membrane is infrastructure. The evidence pages are infrastructure. The cross-links are infrastructure. And infrastructure is morally neutral — it can carry clean water or sewage, evidence or propaganda, transparency or opacity.

The only question about infrastructure is: what does it carry?

Corollary 8: If You've Read This Far, You Are Now Part of the Graph

You arrived here through some path — a search engine, a cross-link, a shared URL, a direct visit. That path is an edge. You are now a node. Your classification depends on what you do next.

If you verify a claim, you harden a classification. If you find an error, you soften one. If you do nothing, you are null — present in the graph, unclassified, still.

What follows: The graph is not a thing we built. It is a thing that grows through interaction. Every reader changes it. Every reader IS it. The investigation is not a publication — it is a surface. And surfaces change when touched.

The Cycle

Thesis: the evidence is real. Antithesis: what if we're wrong? Synthesis: here's what we know, what we don't, and where we're borrowing. Corollary: if any of it is true, these things also follow.

The cycle doesn't end. It goes around. Each pass makes the investigation more honest, not more certain. More honest about where the evidence is strong and where it's thin. More honest about where the investigators' biases might be baked into the architecture. More honest about the things that follow whether we intended them or not.

A corollary doesn't ask permission. It just follows.

If the thesis is true, the antithesis is necessary. If the antithesis is true, the synthesis is necessary. If any of it is true, the corollaries are inevitable. This is how knowledge works. It goes around.

entry.title: Antithesis — What If We Are the Pattern?
entry.content:
The Obligation to Be Wrong

Every investigation that doesn't try to destroy itself is propaganda.

This page is the sharpest knife we could find, pointed inward. Not at the evidence — the evidence is sourced, timestamped, and independently verifiable. At the investigators. At the method. At the assumptions so deep in the architecture that we stopped noticing them.

The synthesis reflects on what we know and don't know. This page asks: what if the knowing itself is the problem?

What If the Pattern Is Noise?

The human brain is a pattern-completion engine. Show it three data points and it will draw you a line. Show it noise and it will find faces. This is called apophenia — the perception of meaningful connections between unrelated things. Its visual cousin is pareidolia — seeing the Virgin Mary on toast.

We see a 5-layer regulatory capture template repeated across MDE, FCC, and AGC. We see money flowing Walton → Martin → Banks in three hops. We see Dykema's phone number on SDJ's IRS filing.

But:

The 5-layer template might just be how all regulation works. Every industry has a regulator, every regulator has a budget, every budget creates dependence on the regulated. That's not a secret conspiracy — it's public choice economics. We might be documenting gravity and calling it corruption.

The money flow from Walton to Martin to Banks passes through foundations that fund hundreds of organizations. We traced three hops because we were looking for three hops. The Walton Family Foundation gave $595 million to education in 2024 alone. Three hops from Walton reaches almost everyone in education.

Dykema is one of the largest law firms in Michigan. Their phone number appears on hundreds of filings. Finding it on one more is not evidence of conspiracy — it's evidence of market share.

The counterargument: We may be documenting the normal shape of the world and presenting it as evidence of capture.

What If We Are the Dark Money?

The investigation criticizes:

  • Anonymity: Domains By Proxy hides the owners of websites targeting individuals
  • Coordination: Multiple PACs governed by the same compliance specialist
  • Targeting: Evidence published about named individuals based on public records
  • Cross-platform amplification: Evidence spread across multiple nodes in the primals.eco network
  • Pseudonymous funding: Dark money vehicles whose donors can't be traced

Now describe the investigation:

  • Anonymity: This site has no individual author's name on it
  • Coordination: Multiple primals.eco nodes operated from a shared infrastructure
  • Targeting: Evidence published about named individuals based on public records
  • Cross-platform amplification: Evidence spread across multiple nodes in the primals.eco network
  • Pseudonymous funding: The investigation's funding and operational structure are not disclosed

Read both lists again. They are structurally identical.

The investigation argues that anonymity + coordination + targeting = something worth documenting when done by the other side. If so, it is worth documenting when done by this side. The First Amendment protects both. The ethics of both deserve the same scrutiny.

The counterargument: We are a mirror. And a mirror cannot claim to be different from the thing it reflects.

What If 94% Dismissal Is Correct?

The investigation's flagship statistic: the AGC dismisses 94% of complaints.

We present this as evidence of systemic failure. But:

  • Most complaints to any professional licensing body are meritless. The State Bar of California dismisses ~80%. The AMA dismisses similar percentages of medical complaints. This is normal.
  • Attorney-client privilege means the AGC often cannot investigate without the complainant's attorney waiving privilege — which they rarely do.
  • Many complaints are filed by the opposing party in litigation and are tactical, not substantive.
  • The AGC's mandate is to protect the public, not to adjudicate disputes between litigants.

What would a 50% action rate look like? It would mean the AGC acts on every other complaint. That would include the ones filed out of spite, the ones filed because someone lost a case, and the ones filed by people who don't understand the attorney's ethical obligations. It would be chaos.

The counterargument: The dismissal rate might be evidence of triage, not failure. We assumed failure because we're the ones filing complaints.

What If the Children Are Fine?

MacDowell Preparatory Academy: 3% math proficiency. We present this as an indictment.

But:

  • The comparison schools in the same zip code might have 4% or 7% — not dramatically different. Detroit's district-wide proficiency rates hover in single digits.
  • Proficiency is measured by standardized tests that have their own well-documented biases.
  • The parents at PCA chose that school. Parental choice is the foundational argument for charter schools, and dismissing the parents' choice is dismissing the parents.
  • Some of the students at PCA might be thriving in ways the tests don't measure — stability, belonging, safety, adult relationships.

The counterargument: We might be weaponizing test scores against Black children at Black-led schools while using the vocabulary of civil rights to do it. This is a real risk. It is the risk that the DeVos/Walton critique of accountability systems is sometimes correct even if their proposed alternative is self-serving.

What If Null Is the Answer?

The synthesis identifies 100 null entities — things the investigation couldn't classify — and frames them as problems to solve. "Jiggle that which is still."

But what if null is the answer?

Dykema is null because it serves both sides. That's what a law firm does. Classifying Dykema as self or non-self would be classifying the practice of law itself. A firm that serves both sides is supposed to be null. Forcing classification on it would be forcing the world to take a side, and the world doesn't owe us sides.

Renae Moore governs 6 PACs across both parties. She is a compliance specialist. Her job is to file paperwork correctly regardless of ideology. She is null because she is doing her job. Classifying her as non-self because she also does paperwork for entities we're investigating would be classifying administrative competence as malice.

Kenneth Griffin donates to political causes. He is interstitial because his money passes through the system without him directing the specific entities at the local level. He is null because the causal chain between his donation and a specific charter school in Detroit passes through so many intermediaries that the connection is atmospheric, not architectural.

The counterargument: Some things are genuinely unclassifiable. Not because we lack evidence — because the classification itself is a category error. Demanding that every entity be self or non-self is demanding that the universe be binary. It isn't.

What If the Membrane Is a Cage?

The membrane protects. 97% selectivity. 92.6% reflection. 0 real content to fleet. We celebrate these numbers.

But:

  • Selectivity is censorship. We decide what gets through and what doesn't. We call our decisions "immune response." The people we're documenting call their decisions the same thing.
  • Reflection is an echo chamber. If 92.6% of traffic bounces back, the remaining 7.4% is self-selected for agreement. The membrane creates an audience that already believes us.
  • Opsonization is mob tagging. When humans tag entities on the site, we call it "collective intelligence." When people tag others on social media for coordinated action, we call it harassment. The mechanism is identical.
  • 0 content to fleet means fleet gets nothing. But fleet is not monolithic. Some of that fleet is Google's crawler trying to index us for search. Some of it is archive.org trying to preserve us. Some of it is researchers trying to study us. We don't distinguish — we reflect all of them.

The counterargument: The membrane is architecture, and all architecture constrains. The question is not whether it constrains — it's whether we are honest about what it constrains and who it excludes.

What If We Just Like This?

The darkest counterargument. Not an intellectual one.

What if the investigation persists not because the evidence demands it, but because the investigators enjoy it? What if the dopamine hit of finding another connection, tracing another hop, writing another article is what drives the work — not accountability?

What if the investigation has become self-sustaining — a system that generates its own fuel by finding more things to investigate, which generates more connections, which generates more things to investigate?

What if we are, in the most literal sense, addicted to the pattern?

The counterargument: Enjoyment is not evidence of error. A scientist who loves her microscope is not biased by her love. But a scientist who cannot stop looking through the microscope — who sees everything as a specimen — has a problem. The question is whether the investigation has an off switch. Whether it can look at an entity and say "this is not suspicious, this is just a person doing their job" and mean it.

The Responses (Not Defenses)

These are not arguments to be defeated. They are arguments to be held.

To the pattern-is-noise argument: Yes. Some of what we see might be the normal shape of the world. The safeguard is sourcing — every claim linked to a specific document, docket, or filing. Pattern alone is not evidence. Pattern plus public record is.

To the we-are-dark-money argument: Yes. Structurally, we resemble what we document. The difference is that our output is public record, our evidence is verifiable, and our subjects can respond on the same site (opsonization). Dark money vehicles produce no public record. But the structural similarity is real and we should not pretend otherwise.

To the 94%-is-correct argument: Maybe. We don't know the base rate of meritorious complaints. What we know is that specific, documented, sourced complaints — with named witnesses, case numbers, and evidence — were dismissed without explanation. The aggregate rate might be fine. The specific cases we documented are not fine.

To the children-are-fine argument: This one cuts. Test scores are not destiny. Parental choice matters. And the risk of outsiders weaponizing metrics against Black communities in the name of accountability is real and documented. The response is not to stop measuring — it's to measure honestly and include the measurements that matter to the community, not just to the state.

To the null-is-the-answer argument: Sometimes, yes. Dykema might genuinely be null. Moore might genuinely be null. But null is a classification, not an absence of classification. Saying "this entity is genuinely unclassifiable" is different from saying "we haven't tried." The synthesis tracks the difference.

To the membrane-is-cage argument: All architecture constrains. The honest response is to publish the constraint. This page is that publication. The membrane's selectivity rules are documented. The reflection rate is documented. The 0-content-to-fleet policy is documented. Transparency about the cage is not the same as having no cage — but it's the minimum.

To the we-just-like-this argument: Probably true. The safeguard is the public record. If the investigation becomes self-serving, the evidence trail will show it — articles that don't source claims, connections that don't verify, patterns that don't hold up. The evidence is the governor on the engine. When the evidence says stop, we stop.

Why This Page Exists

Because an investigation that never challenges itself is a prosecution.

Because the strongest version of the opposing argument makes the investigation stronger, not weaker — the same way a virus makes the immune system stronger.

Because the people we document deserve to have the best possible case made on their behalf, even if they wouldn't make it themselves.

Because the synthesis asked "what do we know?" and this page asks "what if we're wrong?" — and you need both.

Because thesis, antithesis, synthesis is not a sequence — it's a cycle. You go around. And around. And the investigation is honest about every lap.

Every investigation owes itself the sharpest knife it can find and the courage to point it inward.

This is the knife.

entry.title: The Enforcement Ecosystem — Who Is Supposed to Be Doing This?
entry.content:
The Question

Who has the mandate, the evidence, and the authority to act — and what did they do with it?

This is not an investigation of the network. This is an investigation of the investigators. Every body below has statutory or court-rule authority over some piece of the documented misconduct. Not one of them has the full picture.

Ten Bodies. One Complaint. Two Letters.

On October 7, 2026, Clutch Justice documented the exact moment the enforcement gap becomes visible:

A Michigan resident filed a UPL complaint on August 31. On September 30, the State Bar closed the file — "did not meet the standards set by the UPL Committee." The standards were not identified. On October 1, the AGC returned the filing — Banks "is not a listed attorney." That is the fact that makes the conduct a violation. The remedy offered: a State Bar complaint form, for the office that closed the file the afternoon before.

Two letters. One day apart. Each pointing at the other office.

Put the letters in date order and the problem explains itself.

The Map

1. State Bar of Michigan — UPL Department

Jurisdiction: Unauthorized practice of law by non-lawyers (Rule 16, Supreme Court Rules) Authority: Investigate, recommend prosecution to Board of Commissioners, issue subpoenas

Evidence available:

  • Detroit Police Report 26-0909-0176: Banks identified himself as "attorney" to officers
  • School website: "Dr. Brian Banks, J.D., Ph.D." — never admitted to any bar
  • School name: "Purpose Charter Academy School for Law and Public Service"
  • Serenity Guardianship Services Inc (LARA 802290962): for-profit guardianship firm, sole officer never barred

What happened: File No. 26-UP-51 was administratively closed September 30, 2026. The closure letter says the matter "did not meet the standards set by the UPL Committee." The standards are not published. The letter does not say what the investigation consisted of or whether anyone reviewed the police report.

MCL 600.916 has three prohibitions. The third — "shall not in any manner whatsoever represent or designate himself as an attorney" — requires no client, no legal advice, no fee. Telling police officers you are an attorney, and watching them escort a father off school property on that representation, is the conduct the statute was written to prevent.

2. Attorney Grievance Commission (AGC)

Grievance Administrator: Michael V. Goetz (appointed Sep 2019) Deputy Administrator: Kimberly L. Uhuru Asst Deputy Administrator: Cynthia C. Bullington (at AGC since 1982 — 44 years) Jurisdiction: Attorney misconduct — licensed attorneys only Staff: 13 attorneys, 3 investigators

Evidence available:

  • Lisa Moreland: AAG who argued against Banks' administrator certificate → became PCA Board Director AND Banks' litigation attorney (MRPC 1.7 conflict)
  • Gregory Meihn: Attorney retained within 14 minutes of MDE investigation notification
  • Verkeydia Hall: Filed PPO against journalist investigating Banks
  • The complainant wrote to AG Nessel about Moreland's dual role on September 10. No response.

What happened: The AGC returned the Banks UPL filing on October 1. Cynthia Bullington's letter notes Banks is not a listed attorney and encloses a State Bar complaint form.

The gap: The supplemental complaint also addressed licensed attorneys (Moreland, Meihn, Hall). The return letter addresses only Banks. It is silent on the licensed attorneys who ARE within AGC jurisdiction.

As documented in the Institutional Immunity Pattern, the AGC's own annual reports show:

  • 2024: 88.8% of dispositions dismissed (1,627/1,832)
  • 2023: 72.2% dismissed at intake
  • 2012–2020: Three of every four complaints dismissed by the Grievance Administrator before reaching a hearing panel

3. Attorney Discipline Board (ADB)

Chair: Peter A. Smit (Oct 2026 – Sep 2027) Executive Director: Wendy A. Neeley Function: Adjudicates attorney discipline cases prosecuted by the AGC

The structural problem: Jehan Crump-Gibson is an ADB Hearing Panelist (appointed May 2017). Hearing panelists sit on three-member panels that conduct evidentiary hearings in attorney discipline cases.

Crump-Gibson simultaneously:

  • Serves on panels that adjudicate attorney misconduct
  • Represents Banks — a person who is the subject of interconnected attorney misconduct complaints
  • Sits on the CitizenDetroit Action Group board with the DPSCD Board member who authorized Banks' charter

The ADB processes what the AGC sends it. If the AGC doesn't prosecute, the ADB has nothing to adjudicate. The system depends on the AGC acting.

4. Judicial Tenure Commission (JTC)

Interim Executive Director: Glenn J. Page (returned from retirement Feb 1, 2026) Commission Chair: Thomas J. Ryan, Esq. Staff: 15 positions (13 attorneys, 2 admin) — for all judicial oversight in the State of Michigan Phone: (313) 875-5110

Evidence available: Five Wayne County judges with documented connections to the Banks network:

  • Judge Miller — PCA Board Chair while on the bench. Dismissed infant murder case.
  • Judge Yancey — MacDowell Board Chair. Campaign paid $383.82 to Banks Strategy LLC.
  • Judge Aliyah Sabree — MSU Law classmate of Banks' claimed JD cohort.
  • Judge Sean Perkins — Brother of Todd Perkins (Banks' attorney). Previously worked at Perkins Law Group.
  • Judge David Perkins — Family donated to Banks-aligned campaigns.

What happened: The JTC acknowledged five Requests for Investigation on September 24, 2026, and assigned them to staff for review.

What happened next (October 12, 2026): When the same complainant sent an email to 88 institutional recipients — including the JTC — with full evidence links and the 88-person CC line visible, the JTC responded in 23 minutes with a boilerplate: "As you were advised in an email response sent to you on September 21 of this year, the Commission cannot take any action in response to an email message."

The JTC has five open RFIs from this complainant. Staff were assigned. The investigations are pending. Yet the JTC's October 12 response treats the complainant as if they are a stranger emailing general questions.

Compare: Nikki Snyder — a State Board of Education member on the same CC line — responded in 13 minutes with her personal cell phone number. Same evidence. Same email. One institution gave a personal phone number. The other gave a form letter pretending it had never heard of the complainant.

The JTC is not refusing to investigate. The formal complaints are on file. The JTC is refusing to acknowledge, in a reply-all to 88 recipients, that it has open investigations. This is how the Institutional Immunity Pattern operates in real time: process the complaint through the confidential channel, perform the boilerplate on the public channel.

The gap:

  • No permanent Executive Director. Applications closed July 13. As of October 12 — no appointment.
  • Lynn Helland retired "abruptly" January 31, 2026. Clutch Justice flagged the leadership shift and broader questions about the Commission's internal culture.
  • Page returned from retirement — he retired July 2022, came back February 2026.
  • 15 staff for the entire state of Michigan's judicial oversight.
  • Judge Miller is on the ballot November 3, 2026 — 22 days from today.
  • No public proceeding has been initiated.
  • The SBE meets October 13, 2026. Snyder — who responded in 13 minutes — will be in the room.

The same JTC pattern documented in Cross-Subgraph Patterns: Schipper (Barry County) investigation acknowledged, Galen (Eastpointe) confidentially admonished. Different counties, same processing mode.

5. LARA — Corporations Division

LARA Director: Dr. Marlon I. Brown (appointed Feb 2024) Corporations Division Director: Alexis Lupo

Evidence available:

  • 6+ entities in "Not Good" standing or dissolved
  • Purpose Foundation (803294855): 501(c)(3) with two convicted felons in all officer positions
  • Serenity Guardianship (802290962): for-profit guardianship, sole officer never barred
  • SDJ (802002459): three sequential assumed names — Save Detroit Jobs → Impact Detroit → Detroit Leaders

What happened: Automated "Not Good" standing for non-filing. Eventual dissolution for persistent failure.

The gap: LARA's Corporations Division "promotes economic development and growth by facilitating the formation of business entities." Their mandate is facilitation, not oversight. Entity formation is ministerial — if the paperwork is correct, it gets filed. There is no mechanism to cross-reference criminal records against entity officer filings. No mechanism to flag entities where every officer is a convicted felon.

6. Attorney General — Charitable Trust Section

AG: Dana Nessel Contact: ct_email@michigan.gov Jurisdiction: Charitable organization oversight under MCL 400.271 and MCL 14.251

Evidence available:

  • Purpose Foundation (803294855): 501(c)(3), two convicted felons in all officer positions
  • Right Turn Project (800936257): dissolved — were charitable assets properly transferred?

What the AG's office CAN do: The AG just charged Fay Beydoun with 16 felonies for $20M grant abuse at Global Link International. Filed a complaint against Chosen Kingdom Builders for nonprofit governance and fiduciary-duty failures. The AG's office actively prosecutes nonprofit fraud.

What happened here: No public record of action against any Banks network entity.

Purpose Foundation: two convicted felons, $4.9M revenue school, 3% math proficiency, 72.67% of revenue extracted by management company. Global Link: $20M grant, prosecution. The scale is different. The pattern — felon-controlled entity, government funding, inadequate governance — is identical.

7. DPSCD — Office of Charter Schools

Superintendent: Dr. Nikolai Vitti Director of Charter Schools: Kisha Verdusco (since February 2013 — 13 years) Jurisdiction: Charter authorization and oversight under MCL 380.502(4) and 380.507

MCL 380.507(1)(d): "Oversee each public school academy operating under a contract issued by the authorizing body. The oversight must be sufficient to ensure that the board of directors is in compliance with the terms of the contract and with applicable law."

What happened: PCA was authorized in July 2025 despite the operator's bottom- 3% academic record at MacDowell ( 3% math proficiency, statewide rank 1,443/1,488).

DPSCD recently declined to reauthorize Barack Obama Leadership Academy (BOLA). Superintendent Vitti publicly explained that decision by citing "contractual compliance, academic outcomes, and fiscal stewardship." Those same criteria apply to Banks' schools. Different outcome.

PCA's board includes:

  • A sitting judge (Miller) — Board Chair
  • An assistant attorney general (Moreland) — Board Vice Chair
  • A sitting City Council member (Johnson) — Board Secretary

These are DPSCD appointees. Under MCL 380.507, authorizers appoint board members who swear constitutional oaths.

8. Michigan Department of Education

What happened: MDE investigated Banks in February 2022 for having no teaching credential. Application #590606, status: HOLD. Banks continues to operate as superintendent of two schools.

The investigation letter went to Board President Wells-Stallworth. The response: Banks applied for an administrative permit. It was placed on HOLD. No credential has been issued. Banks has continued as superintendent for four years after the investigation.

9. Wayne County Prosecutor

Prosecutor: Kym Worthy

MCL 600.916 makes unauthorized practice of law contempt of the circuit court in the county where it happened. Purpose Charter Academy is in Wayne County. Banks told Wayne County police officers he was an attorney. The complainant asked both the State Bar and AGC to coordinate with the Wayne County Prosecutor. Neither letter mentions doing so.

Worthy herself alleged Judge Miller "displayed a bias" in an infant murder case (WXYZ, 2024). But broader enforcement on the Banks network: no public record of action.

10. Michigan Supreme Court

The Supreme Court:

  • Appoints the Grievance Administrator (Goetz)
  • Appoints the ADB (9 members, including the chair who oversees hearing panelists)
  • Appoints the JTC Commissioners (9 members)
  • Oversees the State Bar's UPL program
  • Declined in 2014 to publish a definition of "the practice of law" for comment

The enforcement system is their creation. When the State Bar closes a holding-out case and the AGC sends it back, the Supreme Court's system produced that outcome. That is not a bug. It is an architectural gap.

The Pattern

BodyHad Evidence?Acted?Result
State Bar UPL✓Closed fileStandards cited, not published
AGC✓Returned re: BanksSilent on licensed attorneys
ADB—Awaiting AGCHearing panelist = defense attorney
JTC✓Acknowledged 5No proceeding. No permanent ED.
LARA✓Automated statusFiling office by design
AG Charitable TrustAvailableNo actionActive on $20M grant fraud elsewhere
DPSCD Charter✓Authorized PCADeclined BOLA under same criteria
MDE✓HOLD on permitNo enforcement beyond letter
Wayne Co Prosecutor✓No actionCoordination requested, not documented
MI Supreme CourtBuilt the system—Declined to define UPL in 2014

Every body exercises authority up to its jurisdictional edge and stops. The edges don't overlap. They gap.

What This Is Not

This is not an allegation of corruption. The Grievance Administrator is following his jurisdiction. The AGC correctly identified that a non-lawyer is outside its scope. The JTC assigned investigations to staff. LARA processes filings. Each body is doing what its mandate says.

The problem is that each mandate was written to handle one actor at a time. The Banks network operates across every mandate simultaneously. An operator who is not a lawyer (State Bar), whose attorneys may have conflicts (AGC), whose board includes judges (JTC), whose entities are controlled by felons (LARA), whose nonprofits hold charitable assets (AG), whose schools are authorized by public bodies (DPSCD), and whose credentials were investigated and left unresolved (MDE). No single body sees the whole pattern. The pattern lives in the gaps.

Connected Analysis

On this site:

  • Hey Mikey, He Likes It! — the man who authored CISPA wants to join the Senate that killed it. Same donors fund Barrett. Same Dykema OS. Same election day. $88.8M from people who don't live in Michigan.

  • Institutional Immunity Pattern — the mathematics of 88.8% dismissal

  • Cross-Subgraph Patterns — same oversight bodies appear across five investigations

  • They Banked on Banks — the man the ecosystem failed to stop. Brian Roderick Banks: 9 convictions, 2 charter schools, board chair is a sitting judge, parent blocked at the door, PPO weaponized. The enforcement ecosystem measured against a live case.

  • Signal Permeability — Live Anderson study: evidence sent to all ten oversight bodies. Measuring who opens it, who forwards it, who ignores it.

On detroit.primals.eco:

  • Data Braid — GLLG Entity Graph — six independent searches converge: defense attorney + charter authorizer on same nonprofit board
  • Corporate Network — LARA — the entity infrastructure
  • Agency Referrals — eight federal agencies, state referrals, JTC investigations

Independent reporting:

  • Mind the Gap: Michigan's Two Lawyer Regulators Pointed at Each Other, One Day Apart (Oct 7, 2026)
  • No One Is Coming (Sep 24, 2026)
  • JTC Names Glenn J. Page Interim Executive Director (Feb 2, 2026)

Verify Everything

ClaimSourceHow to Check
State Bar closed File 26-UP-51Clutch Justice (Oct 7, 2026)Published letter
AGC returned filing Oct 1Clutch Justice (Oct 7, 2026)Published letter
Bullington at AGC since 1982agcmi.org/about-us/our-teamTeam page
JTC interim director since Feb 2026jtc.courts.mi.gov/the_staffStaff page
No permanent JTC ED (apps closed Jul 13)jtc.courts.mi.govNews page
AGC 88.8% dismissal rate (2024)AGC 2024 Annual Reportagcmi.org/documents
MCL 600.916 three prohibitionslegislature.mi.govMCL 600.916(1)
Verdusco at DPSCD since Feb 2013LinkedInProfile
AG charged Beydoun (16 felonies)FOX 2 DetroitPublished report
DPSCD declined BOLAdetroitk12.orgSuperintendent message
ADB members 2026-27adbmich.org/about-us/adb-membersBoard page
Goetz appointment Sep 2019agcmi.org/aboutAbout page

The enforcement system is not broken. It is fragmented. Each body does exactly what its mandate says. The network operates in the space where no mandate reaches. The complainant did everything right. The system produced two letters, one day apart, each pointing at the other door.

entry.title: Hey Mikey, He Likes It! — The Senate Candidate Who Ate Everything They Fed Him
entry.content:
Hey Mikey

You remember the commercial. Two brothers staring at a bowl of cereal. Nobody wants to try it. So they push it at Mikey.

"He likes it! Hey Mikey!"

Mike Rogers is Mikey. The billionaires keep pushing things at him. And he keeps eating.

Surveillance bill that exempts all privacy law? He likes it.

Job from the company whose competitor he investigated? He likes it.

$1.6 million house in Florida while running for Michigan? He likes it.

$88.8M from Texas oil, Blackstone, Citadel, Koch, McConnell, and Musk? He likes it.

Every claim below is sourced to FEC filings, published fact-checks, congressional records, or reporting from Bridge Michigan, PolitiFact, Metro Times, the ACLU, and Business Insider. No private information. No tracking. Verify everything at the bottom.

Who Is Mike Rogers?

FieldValueSource
Full nameMichael J. RogersFEC
BornJune 2, 1963Livingston County, MI
FEC IDS4MI00595fec.gov
CommitteeRogers for Senate (C00849810)FEC
PartyRepublican
Current raceU.S. Senate, Michigan, 2026
OpponentAbdul El-Sayed (D)
ClaimsWhite Lake Township, Oakland County
Also owns$1.6M home, Cape Coral, FLBridge Michigan, Metro Times

The Career

PeriodRoleWhat Happened
1985–1989U.S. Army—
1989–1994FBI Special Agent—
1995–2000Michigan State Senate (District 26)Majority Floor Leader (1999)
2001–2015U.S. House, MI-8Seven terms. Chaired House Intelligence Committee (2011–2015)
2012Authored CISPASurveillance bill exempting ALL privacy law — killed by Senate twice
2012Led Huawei/ZTE investigationHouse Intel Committee found both were national security threats
2015Left CongressDid not seek 8th term
2015+Cumulus Radio hostSyndicated show + CNN commentator
2016–2017AT&T "Chief Security Adviser"AT&T was negotiating with Huawei. Rogers chaired the committee that called Huawei a threat.
2016+Board seatsIronNet Cybersecurity, Nokia, Telefónica, MITRE Corporation
2022Bought $1.6M Cape Coral, FL homeDeclared it permanent residence in 2023
2024First Senate runLost to Elissa Slotkin by ~221,000 votes
Apr 2025Announced 2nd Senate runUnopposed in Aug 4, 2026 GOP primary
Nov 3, 2026Election Day25 days from this publication

Army → FBI → State Senate → Congress → Intel Chair → surveillance bill → revolving door → telecom boards → Florida mansion → Senate run (lost) → Senate run (again).

That is the résumé of a man who has never stopped being fed.

Thing 1: The Surveillance Bill

Rogers authored CISPA — the Cyber Intelligence Sharing and Protection Act. He introduced it twice:

  • H.R. 3523 (112th Congress, 2011–2012)
  • H.R. 624 (113th Congress, 2013–2014)

The House passed it. Twice. The Senate killed it. Twice.

What CISPA Would Do

ProvisionEffect
Exemption to all privacy lawsCompanies share email content, browsing history, PII with government — no user consent required
Complete liability immunityNo accountability for companies that mishandle shared data
"Significant purpose" standardData used for any lawful purpose as long as cybersecurity or national security is "a significant purpose"
NSA/DoD accessMilitary and intelligence agencies access private data without adequate civilian oversight
Permanent programOnly annual inspector general review

This was not a narrow cybersecurity bill. It was a blanket exemption to every privacy protection Americans had.

Who Opposed It

The ACLU called it "fatally flawed" — a "cybersecurity loophole to existing privacy laws."

The Electronic Frontier Foundation opposed it. Reporters Without Borders opposed it. The American Library Association opposed it. The Obama White House threatened a veto. 41 civil liberties organizations signed a joint opposition letter.

Rogers' response to the privacy concerns:

"We feel that the bill clearly deals with privacy, that the checks and balances are there, but [we] know there's still a perception and we're still trying to deal with that."

The ACLU's response:

"Everyone, from the privacy community to the president, agrees that CISPA is bad on privacy — the problem isn't our perception."

The Senate agreed. Both times.

Why This Matters Now

Rogers is running for the Senate. The body that killed his surveillance bill — twice — is the body he wants to join. The committee he would sit on would oversee the same intelligence community CISPA was designed to feed.

The same government apparatus that cannot coordinate UPL enforcement across two offices — sending two letters, one day apart, each pointing at the other door — wanted Rogers-level surveillance authority over every American's private communications.

They couldn't handle two letters. He wanted to give them everyone's email.

Thing 2: The Revolving Door

This one requires a timeline.

YearRogersAT&T
2012House Intelligence Chairman — leads investigation finding Huawei is a national security threat—
2012Publishes report recommending US companies stop doing business with Huawei—
2015Leaves Congress—
2016Hired as AT&T "Chief Security Adviser"Negotiating with Huawei to sell Huawei phones in the US
2017Still at AT&TDeal with Huawei collapses after congressional pressure

Read that again. The man who chaired the committee that declared Huawei a national security threat was hired by the company that was negotiating with Huawei.

The Contradiction

Rogers said: He persuaded AT&T to drop the Huawei deal.

AT&T said: Rogers "had no role in business or purchasing decisions with the company."

AT&T then said: Rogers had no involvement in the Huawei negotiations.

He either had influence (his claim) or he didn't (AT&T's claim). Both cannot be true. One of them is lying.

The Lobbying Pipeline

Two of Rogers' former chiefs of staff were employed at Navigators Global — a lobbying firm that lobbied Congress on AT&T's behalf during the same period Rogers worked for AT&T.

During his House career, AT&T's federal PAC gave Rogers $56,000. Verizon gave $28,500. CTIA (the wireless industry trade group) gave $10,000.

Investigate the entity → leave Congress → get hired by the entity → entity's competitor (that you investigated) negotiates with the entity → deal collapses → you claim credit (or don't).

That is the revolving door. Rogers walked through it. He liked it.

Thing 3: The Florida Problem

DateEventSource
2015Left Congress, eventually left Michigan—
2022Bought $1.6M home, Cape Coral, FLProperty records
2023Declared FL home as permanent residence (homestead tax exemption)Bridge Michigan
Jan 2024MI Advance reported Rogers living at sister-in-law's Brighton houseMI Advance
Apr 2024Still registered to vote in FloridaVoter records
Aug 2024Canceled FL voter registration—
Nov 2025Campaigned from FL home for 10+ daysMetro Times
Nov 2025Told MI radio audience: "my whole life is here [in Michigan]" — while in FloridaMetro Times
Jan 2026Cape Coral listing removed from market (was listed at $2.4M)Realtor.com
CurrentStill owns the Cape Coral propertyProperty records

Bridge Michigan:

"The record is clear. Rogers left Michigan after serving in the US House and later bought a house in Florida in 2022. He and his wife listed the home as their primary residence as recently as 2023."

He declared Florida his permanent residence for the tax break. He was registered to vote in Florida eight months into his first Senate campaign. He campaigned from Florida while telling Michigan he lives in Michigan.

He likes both. Florida for living. Michigan for running.

Thing 4: The Money

What Rogers Raised (FEC, through Jul 15, 2026)

SourceAmount
Individual contributions$6,831,819
PAC contributions$787,227
Transfers from authorized committees$3,166,695
Total raised$10,898,177

Top employers of individual donors: Blackstone, Paradigm, Ford Motor Company.

The CEO of Blackstone gave $4.5 million to Rogers' super PAC. Blackstone employees give to the campaign. Both channels, same source.

What Outside Groups Spent FOR Rogers

CommitteeAmountWho Funds It
Senate Leadership Fund (SLF)$27,421,796McConnell-aligned
No Going Back PAC$22,311,010—
Americans for Prosperity Action$14,154,965Koch network
Great Lakes Conservatives Fund$7,155,673Dunn, Griffin, Schwarzman
America PAC$5,764,178Elon Musk
Sentinel Action Fund$3,077,584$2.5M dark money inflow
Other$2,215,451Various
Total outside money benefiting Rogers$82,100,057

Grand total benefiting Rogers: $88.8M .

Rogers raised $10.9 million himself. Outside groups spent $82.1 million for him. For every dollar Rogers raised, outside groups spent seven.

His opponent — Abdul El-Sayed — has $51.7 million total benefiting (VoteLog). That includes approximately $20.1 million from United Democracy Project (AIPAC's super PAC) opposing El-Sayed. Outside money doesn't just flow in one direction. It flows in every direction. Billionaires fund Rogers. A foreign-policy lobby targets his opponent. Michigan voters are the smallest voice in their own Senate race.

This is not a page about Rogers vs. El-Sayed. Both candidates are swimming in outside money. This is a page about what Rogers' record says — CISPA, AT&T, Florida, $88.8M — because the record is what voters can verify. El-Sayed's record is his to answer for. Rogers' record is documented below.

Who Feeds the Machine

Great Lakes Conservatives Fund (GLCF)

FEC ID: C00853861. Registered October 17, 2023. Super PAC (Independent Expenditure-Only).

DonorAmountWhere From
Tim Dunn (CrownQuest Operating)~$10,000,000Midland, Texas
Stephen Schwarzman (Blackstone)$4,500,000New York
Kenneth Griffin (Citadel)$2,500,000Miami, Florida
Michael Psaros (KPS Capital Partners)$50,000New York
Albert Hegyi (1st Financial Bank USA)$25,000—

$17 million from three men. None of them lives in Michigan.

Tim Dunn is a Texas oil executive. He gave $10 million to elect a Michigan senator. He does not live in Michigan. He does not vote in Michigan. He runs CrownQuest Operating in Midland, Texas — a town named after oil.

Stephen Schwarzman runs Blackstone — the world's largest alternative investment firm. He maxed out to Barrett too.

Kenneth Griffin runs Citadel — one of the world's largest hedge funds. He also gave $7,000 to Barrett. Same donor. Senate AND House. Cross-ticket.

The cross-ticket signal: Griffin and Schwarzman both fund Rogers (Senate) AND Barrett (MI-7). The infrastructure is not candidate-specific. It is party-wide.

The Shared Treasurer

Rhinoceros Media found that Rogers' campaign and the James federal campaign share a treasurer (Crosby Ottenhoff / Kirsten Quick). The money flows through shared infrastructure.

Thing 5: The Dykema Connection

No direct FEC contribution from Dykema Gossett to Rogers' federal campaign was found. But Dykema doesn't need to write checks to Rogers. Dykema builds the infrastructure that everyone uses.

Dykema Gossett plays both sides at state level:

RecipientAmount
Senate Republican Campaign Committee$9,500
Michigan Senate Democratic Fund$7,500
House Republican Campaign Committee$7,500
Michigan House Democratic Fund$8,000

Both parties. All four caucuses. The operating system doesn't pick winners. It builds the machine.

Dykema is the same firm that:

  • Formed Save Detroit Jobs (LARA 802002459) — the dark money vehicle whose president is a convicted federal felon
  • SDJ's IRS filing lists Dykema's office phone number
  • SDJ funded Latisha Johnson's City Council campaign — Johnson sits on the PCA Board as Secretary
  • For the full architecture: How To Build an OS →

Rogers sits atop the same ticket infrastructure that Barrett plugs into. Griffin funds both. Schwarzman funds both. Dykema serves both. Same operating system. Different executables.

Thing 6: Same Election Day

November 3, 2026. Four candidates. One date. One infrastructure.

RaceCandidateConnection
U.S. SenateMike Rogers (R) $88.8M total. GLCF, AFP, SLF, America PAC. Griffin + Schwarzman.
U.S. House MI-7Tom Barrett (R)Dykema PAC → $4,000 . Griffin $7,000 . Schwarzman maxed. NRCC $6,300,000 .
Wayne County 3rd CircuitJudge Cylenthia MillerPCA Board Chair. JTC investigating. On the ballot.
36th District CourtJudge Tenisha YanceyMacDowell Board Chair. Paid $383.82 to Banks Strategy LLC.

Different levels. Different races. Same day. Same donor base. Same dark money infrastructure. Same enforcement ecosystem that can't coordinate two letters.

Miller and Yancey sit on school boards with a man with 9 criminal convictions who calls himself an attorney. The JTC is investigating. The election is in 25 days.

Barrett calls tenant organizers felons while his donor's dark money entity is run by an actual felon. The election is in 25 days.

Rogers authored America's most aggressive surveillance bill, got hired by the company whose competitor he investigated, bought a house in Florida, and accepted $88.8M from people who don't live in Michigan. The election is in 25 days.

Same system. Same day. Different wrappers.

The $30,000 Question

Before leaving Congress, Rogers received $30,000 from CGCN Group — a lobbying firm with 50+ clients including pharmaceutical and medical technology companies. After leaving Congress, Rogers' net worth grew by an estimated $14 million or more (Business Insider).

Army salary → FBI salary → State Senate salary → congressional salary → board seats + consulting → net worth measured in eight figures.

They keep feeding him. He keeps eating.

Wave Propagation

HOUSE INTEL CHAIR (2011–2015)
    │
    ├── CISPA ──► exemption to all privacy law ──► killed by Senate (twice)
    │
    ├── HUAWEI INVESTIGATION ──► "national security threat"
    │       │
    │       └── LEFT CONGRESS ──► hired by AT&T ──► AT&T negotiating with Huawei
    │               │
    │               └── Two former chiefs of staff lobby for AT&T via Navigators Global
    │
    ├── BOARD SEATS ──► IronNet / Nokia / Telefónica / MITRE
    │       │
    │       └── Net worth +$14M since leaving Congress
    │
    └── 2024 SENATE RUN (LOST) ──► 2026 SENATE RUN
            │
            ├── GLCF: Dunn $10M + Schwarzman $4.5M + Griffin $2.5M
            ├── AFP (Koch): $14.2M
            ├── SLF (McConnell): $27.4M
            ├── America PAC (Musk): $5.8M
            │
            └── Same Nov 3 election as Barrett (MI-7) + Miller + Yancey
                    │
                    └── Same Dykema infrastructure serves all of them

One career. One direction. Always upward. Always fed.

Verify Everything

ClaimSourceHow to Check
Rogers FEC fundraisingFECfec.gov/data/candidate/S4MI00595/
GLCF donors and spendingFEC Schedule Adocquery.fec.gov → C00853861
CISPA text and oppositionACLU, Congress.govH.R. 3523 (112th), H.R. 624 (113th)
AT&T employment 2016–17PolitiFact, Business InsiderPublished fact-checks
AT&T contradictory statementsPolitiFact2024 fact-check
Florida residencyBridge MichiganPublished investigation
FL voter registration Apr 2024MI AdvancePublished report
Campaigned from FL Nov 2025Metro TimesPublished report
Outside spending totalsVoteLogvotelog.org
GLCF total spendFEC IE filingsFEC independent expenditure search
Shared treasurerRhinoceros Mediarhinocerosmedia.org
Net worth growth post-CongressBusiness InsiderPublished Feb 2024
Dykema state PAC bipartisanTransparencyUSAtransparencyusa.org
CGCN Group $30KFECDisbursement search
El-Sayed total benefitingVoteLogvotelog.org
Griffin → Barrett $7,000 FECCommittee C00793976
Schwarzman → Barrett maxedFEC, Rhinoceros MediaPublished reporting

Connected Analysis

On this site:

  • The Enforcement Ecosystem — The ten oversight bodies Rogers' Senate seat would influence. They can't coordinate two letters. He wanted to give them everyone's email.

  • Tommy Boy — Barrett shares donors (Griffin, Schwarzman) and infrastructure (Dykema). Same ticket. Same day. Same system.

  • Sitting in a Tree — The complete picture: Mike and Tom and Dykema and Banks. One law firm, one compliance specialist, four branches. Same tree, same roots, same Renae Moore watering all of it.

  • How To Build an OS — The Dykema architecture both candidates plug into.

  • Institutional Immunity — The 88.8% dismissal rate at the AGC that Rogers' oversight role would perpetuate.

  • Cross-Subgraph Patterns — Same oversight failures, five counties, one system.

  • They Banked on Banks — Brian Roderick Banks: 9 convictions, 2 charter schools, board chaired by Judge Miller. Same ballot day. Same system. The convicted felon the system protects.

  • Signal Permeability — Live Anderson study: does the evidence propagate through oversight boundaries, or localize?

On detroit.primals.eco:

  • The Network — The charter school network connected to Miller, Yancey, and Banks — all on the same ballot, same day, same infrastructure.
  • Brian Roderick Banks — Full Profile — 9 convictions, credential chain, entity control, email admissions.
  • Data Braid — GLLG — Six independent searches converge on the defense attorney + charter authorizer sitting on the same nonprofit board.
  • Agency Referrals — Eight federal agencies, state referrals, JTC investigations. The enforcement ecosystem in action — or inaction.

Every claim on this page is sourced to FEC filings, congressional records, published reporting from Bridge Michigan, PolitiFact, Metro Times, MI Advance, CNN, NYT, Business Insider, the ACLU, and Rhinoceros Media. No private information is disclosed. No tracking. No cookies.

Hey Mikey. He likes it. He likes everything they feed him. The surveillance bill. The revolving door. The Florida mansion. The $88.8M . The seat in the body that killed his bill twice.

He'll eat anything.

This is not an endorsement. This is not a recommendation. This is a record. We don't pick sides. We refute falsity. When Rogers says "my whole life is here" from a Florida living room, that is falsity. When his campaign says he had no role in AT&T decisions while he says he persuaded them, one of those is falsity. When $82 million in outside money speaks for a candidate, that is a fact Michigan voters should see — regardless of party.

Nov 3, 2026. Read the record. Verify it. Vote your conscience.

entry.title: Signal Permeability — Live Anderson Study of Institutional Response
entry.content:
The Experiment

At 4:43 PM EDT on October 9, 2026, an email was sent from a secure address to recipients including oversight bodies, journalists, and enforcement contacts. The email contained links to documented evidence about Brian Roderick Banks — a man with 9 criminal convictions operating two publicly funded charter schools in Detroit.

The email contained:

  • A link to "They Banked on Banks" — the full analysis
  • A link to "The Enforcement Ecosystem" — the ten oversight bodies that should be acting
  • Links to detroit.primals.eco — the 287-page evidence library
  • Links to independent reporting (Clutch Justice, Detroit Free Press)
  • Verification instructions (State Bar search, ICHAT, LARA, PCA board page)

Then we watched.

Not whether the evidence is convincing — it is independently verifiable in minutes. We watched whether the system is permeable to evidence at all.

Anderson Localization — The Physics

In condensed matter physics, Anderson localization describes how disorder in a medium prevents wave propagation. In an ordered crystal, an electron wave propagates freely. Add enough disorder — random potentials, structural defects — and the wave becomes trapped. It doesn't reach the other side.

The metaphor is precise:

PhysicsOversight System
WaveEvidence signal
Ordered crystalFunctioning oversight cascade
DisorderJurisdictional gaps, conflicts of interest, institutional inertia
PropagationEvidence reaches decision-maker, action follows
LocalizationSignal is absorbed, ignored, or redirected — no action

If the oversight system is permeable, the signal propagates: evidence reaches investigators, investigators act, children are protected. If the system exhibits Anderson localization, the signal dies at each boundary — absorbed, reflected, or scattered into jurisdictional gaps.

This page is the measurement.

The Signal — October 9, 2026

T+0:00 — Signal Emitted (20:43 UTC)

Email sent from secure address. Contains documented evidence:

  • Brian Roderick Banks: 9 convictions (ICHAT SID 2029469K)
  • False attorney claim (DPD Report #26-0909-0176)
  • Parent custody access denied at school
  • PPO filed against parent who complained
  • Board chair is a sitting judge in the court that processes the PPO
  • 3% math proficiency, 72.67% revenue extraction

T+0:36 — First Permeability Confirmation (20:44:03 UTC)

Barracuda Email Security Service scans the Banks article link.

Source: outbound-ip47b.ess.barracuda.com (209.222.82.235)
Target: /analysis/they-banked-on-banks/
Response: HTTP 200, 21,523 bytes (full article)
Verdict: Link marked SAFE → email delivered to recipient inbox

What this proves: The email reached at least one recipient protected by Barracuda ESS (Enterprise cloud email security). Barracuda fetched the full 21,523-byte article, confirmed it was safe, and delivered the email. The signal crossed the first membrane.

Barracuda ESS customers include Michigan state agencies, school districts, law enforcement, and enterprise organizations.

T+1:34 — Signal Amplification (20:45:17 UTC)

AWS link preview bot (us-east-1) fetches the Banks article.

Source: ec2-3-236-46-40.compute-1.amazonaws.com
Target: /analysis/they-banked-on-banks/
Response: HTTP 200, 20 bytes (HEAD-like preview)

Interpretation: The recipient who received the email copied the link and pasted it into a messaging platform (Slack, Microsoft Teams, Discord). The platform's link preview bot fetched the URL to render a preview card.

The signal was forwarded. The first recipient shared it with someone else.

T+1:35 — Parallel Amplification (20:45:18 UTC)

AWS link preview bot (us-east-2, Ohio) fires 4 rapid requests.

Source: ec2-18-225-181-43.us-east-2.compute.amazonaws.com
Target: /analysis/they-banked-on-banks/ (×4)
Response: HTTP 200, 6,938 bytes each
Timing: 4 hits in 0.087 seconds

Ohio. The article was shared to a platform whose infrastructure runs in Ohio — one state away from Michigan.

T+1:51–2:09 — Enforcement Ecosystem Activation (20:45:26–20:45:33 UTC)

Five IPs from four different networks simultaneously fetch the Enforcement Ecosystem article:

TimeIPNetworkPage
20:45:2662.10.205.18EU Cloud/analysis/enforcement-ecosystem/
20:45:2662.10.205.21EU Cloud (paired)/analysis/enforcement-ecosystem/
20:45:3272.153.231.12Microsoft (Redmond)/analysis/enforcement-ecosystem/
20:45:33135.232.20.12RIPE/Amsterdam/analysis/enforcement-ecosystem/

All fetched CSS and favicon — the behavioral signature of a real browser render or high-fidelity preview.

The enforcement-ecosystem article was linked in the email. Multiple systems are rendering it simultaneously. The signal is reaching the page that names the ten oversight bodies.

T+4:39 — Cross-Article Amplification (20:48:02 UTC)

AWS bot (us-east-1) fires 6 requests in 0.265 seconds — hitting both articles:

Source: ec2-54-145-141-129.compute-1.amazonaws.com
Targets:
  /analysis/they-banked-on-banks/ (×3)
  /analysis/enforcement-ecosystem/ (×3)
Timing: 6 hits in 0.265 seconds — sub-10ms inter-arrival

Someone shared both links in the same message. A second share event. The signal is being forwarded with both articles together — the evidence AND the enforcement map.

T+11:52 — Detroit Crossover (20:55:19 UTC)

AWS bot (us-east-1, Virginia) fetches a page on detroit.primals.eco:
